title: architecture
Design Philosophy

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/design-philosophy.md — read whole.

- **Radically modular, embeddable engine** — the engine is a set of separately usable crates around a headless DOM that external code drives and any renderer can paint; painting assumes styles and layout are already resolved, and CI guarantees only latest stable, keeping an MSRV check and making an effort not to raise the MSRV in a patch version.

- **Embedder services are injected, with no-op defaults** — networking, navigation, shell and parsing reach the DOM only through provider traits the embedder supplies; script fetches go through the embedder's net provider, never an internal HTTP client.
- **Behave like a browser, and cite the spec** — web semantics are written against named specifications and named browser engines.

- **One incremental pipeline, safe identities** — style, damage, box construction, layout and paint topology are invalidated incrementally through a single code path, over versioned node ids: both layout modes produce identical layouts, a dropped node's id stops resolving instead of aliasing a reused slot, the slotmap key is used only at the storage boundary and every public API takes `NodeId`, and persistent interaction state references DOM nodes only, never layout-generated nodes.

- **Headless, measurable, testable** — the engine is exercised without a window through a headless harness, a WPT runner and phase-split benchmarks; the reference browser keeps its own state best-effort, `HistoryService` the single entry point for its visit and favicon writes, and a loaded document's chrome writes run as one straight-line block so a render cannot sample a half-applied state.

title: Stack and Technologies

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/stack-and-technologies.md — read whole.

The stack: a Rust 2024 Cargo workspace (rust-version 1.91.0) on Servo Stylo, html5ever and xml5ever, Taffy, Parley with ICU4X, anyrender over Vello and Skia, winit, AccessKit, Boa, Dioxus 0.7, tokio and reqwest, with rusqlite in the browser app and Trunk for wasm; GitHub Actions CI runs fmt, clippy, rustdoc, cargo-deny and coverage gates, beside a host-run mutation tier and a Nix flake.

Two keyboard-types versions stand in the graph, Dioxus carrying its own 0.7, so a module that glob-imports `dioxus::prelude::*` names the workspace's crate as `::keyboard_types`; the `ci-scripts` leg needs Python 3.11 or later; mimalloc is the global allocator of two upstream-only binaries, the browser app (by default) and the WPT runner.

Example fixtures under `examples/assets` are standalone HTML documents with no build manifest, source module or config, referencing external assets; the Preact TodoMVC page loads vendored, unmodified Preact builds.

title: Established Decisions

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/established-decisions.md — read whole.

- **[Dependency pinning]** the parser crates match stylo's web_atoms version, skrifa matches parley and vello and svgtypes usvg; taffy and parley are registry versions, so no git dependency is left in the manifest; winit is pinned exactly to a beta, and examples pin `idna_adapter` to disable unicode URL support.

- **[Build profiles]** `dev` sets `debug = "line-tables-only"`, one debuginfo level for the dev host and CI that the `test` profile inherits; named profiles `profile`, `production`, `p2`, `small`, `small-panic` and `tiny`, five crates kept at opt-level 3.
- **[MSRV]** The MSRV job runs only `cargo build`, to avoid requiring dev-dependencies to build with the MSRV (.github/workflows/ci.yml:)

- **[Release versioning]** main is always a prepatch until 1.0, the version in git one minor bump ahead of the actual release; blitz packages are versioned together through the one workspace version and the in-repo `=` pins, and no in-repo release tool remains.

- **[Nix packaging]** The flake builds deps and crate in one derivation (`cargoArtifacts = null`), commenting that the workspace root is a virtual manifest with no root `[package]` (flake.nix:), while the root manifest declares a `[package]` named blitz-examples (Cargo.toml:); checks are disabled in package builds "to avoid building deps for them" (flake.nix:)
- **[Cross-compilation]** `cross` is installed from a git rev because the latest release does not work with recent Rust when targeting Android (.github/workflows/ci.yml:)

- **[Renderer backends]** `paint_bench` runs vello (default), vello_cpu or vello_hybrid; `screenshot` and the test harness's `screenshot` render through `VelloCpuImageRenderer`, the harness compositing over opaque white; wpt defaults to cpu; rdme selects one renderer per feature; `dioxus-native` raises a `compile_error!` when no renderer is enabled.

- **[Default features]** each crate fixes its default feature set in its manifest — blitz-dom: svg, woff, accessibility, system-fonts, file-input, custom-widget, text-transform-icu; `writing-mode` is in no default list; `woff` is default-on in dioxus-native so wasm callers can bundle compressed fonts; the `net` feature is a no-op on wasm32.

- **[Style threading]** `StyleThreading` derives `Default` with `#[default] Sequential` (packages/blitz-dom/src/config.rs:), and the `style_threading` field doc names `Sequential` the default (packages/blitz-dom/src/config.rs:); `Parallel` traversals are serialised process-wide by the static `PARALLEL_TRAVERSAL_LOCK`, its poison recovered with no panic path, so two documents resolving `Parallel` concurrently on Stylo's global pool no longer panic (blitz issue 430) (packages/blitz-dom/src/config.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:); the windowed `dioxus_native::launch` and the browser's document loader and toolbar build their documents `Parallel`, and no headless document — harness, stand or driver — sets `style_threading` (packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:; packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:; apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs:; apps/browser/src/toolbar.rs:); `Sequential` bypasses Stylo's global thread pool (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:); a thread-local `LAYOUT_CTX` carries a FIXME that it is not necessarily correct in a multi-document context (packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:)

- **[Document defaults]** incremental layout on, CSS media type `screen`, documents always HTML in no-quirks mode, a fixed set of Stylo prefs enabled, an empty `data:` default `DocumentUrl`, and headless documents and the WPT viewport in `ColorScheme::Light`.

- **[Resource loading]** `<head>` stylesheets are render-blocking and `resolve` returns before styling while any are pending; iframe nesting is capped at 10 and nested `@import` at 16; `srcdoc` takes precedence over `src`; loaded images are cached by URL, concurrent requests queued on one fetch; author stylesheets are ordered by owner node id.

- **[Fonts]** `@font-face` fonts are registered under the CSS-declared family, weight and style rather than the file's metadata (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); `local()` sources are not supported (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:); SVG and EOT fonts are skipped, and WOFF/WOFF2 without `woff` (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:); default generic base size is 13px monospace, 16px otherwise (packages/blitz-dom/src/font_metrics.rs:); `font-feature-settings` is appended after `font-variant-*` features so it takes precedence (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_parley.rs:); generic family `None` maps to sans-serif (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_parley.rs:); `-apple-system` and `BlinkMacSystemFont` map to system-ui on Apple targets (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_parley.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_parley.rs:)

- **[CSS approximations]** where Stylo or Taffy lack a feature the engine approximates it — CSSOM geometry snapped to 1/64 px, `display: table` laid out as Taffy grid, `overflow: auto` as scroll, `scrollbar_width` 0, sizing keywords on min/max size as auto, baseline alignment falling back to start/end, and like mappings.

- **[Unsupported features]** Shadow DOM, container queries, 3D transforms (a z-axis rotate applied as planar), CSS `offset` in transforms, visited-link styling, anchor positioning, grid subgrid and masonry, non-string pseudo-element `content` and anonymous table wrapper boxes; `:focus-visible`, `:valid`, `:invalid`, `:required` and `:target` always match false, while `:focus-within` matches by element state.

- **[Scrolling and input]** root scroll applies to the viewport; `overflow: hidden` scrolls programmatically only; user scrolls chain to the viewport, `scroll_to` and `scroll_by` clamp to one box; `scroll_into_view` writes every scrolling box on the chain, nested ones instantly, so it never animates a nested box; a box's client rect never subtracts its own scroll offset, and a hit stops at the padding box of every box paint clips; where a select list stands open a hit answers the list first, with no scrollbar, so a row lies past any box that clips its select, a wheel over the list scrolls the list, and `scroll_into_view` on a row writes the list's `scroll_y` at once and moves no chain or viewport.

- Those two fixes, the accessibility builder's state writes and the range input, keyboard activation and focus rules are direct engine changes for every document, each flagged upstreamable with no upstream pull request open.

- Beside those, seven more direct engine changes for every document, the document's clock — every engine time read goes through `DocumentConfig.clock`, wall time when it is unset — and the select model of keys, typeahead and click, and eight more — `visible_region` through transforms, a non-invertible transform's no hit, the focus fixup under `inert`, the tree's focus falling back to the window, native `toggled`, the `multiple` select, `optgroup` and `change` on a checkbox and a radio — each flagged upstreamable with no upstream pull request open; the merge surface of those eight is a line owned by Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration, `hit_inner` a textual conflict with upstream `0980cce5f`.

- The select list is one more direct engine change for every document, remote pages included, ratified; its merge surface is the sixteen files of `escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-select-popup/evidence/merge-surface.md`, a line owned by Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration.

- The twelve commits of the upstream take read at `e42ee1f25` are engine behaviour changes for every document, ratified for their take; the key-press panic's fix, `BaseDocument::deallocate_anonymous_block` setting `layout_parent` to `None` on each child still naming the block, is one more direct engine change for every document, ratified, flagged upstreamable with nothing sent upstream, its merge surface a line owned by Upstream sync ahead of determinism and exploration.

- The select model: every choice that changes the chosen option or a `multiple` select's chosen set goes through the one path `apply_select_choice`, and a single select's choice of its chosen option fires nothing; a `multiple` select and an `optgroup`'s options are modelled in the keys, pointer, form, tree, sheet, snapshot and bridge; a click, Enter and a Space with no typed text standing open a single select's list, which the engine paints over the page with a group's `label` as a header, and a bound label's click focuses the select and opens nothing; an option of a closed single select, under a group too, takes no click and stays refused `covered`; a `multiple` select's `size` hints its height, a single select's stays unread, and Ctrl+A is not modelled.

- **[Selection, animation, pseudo-elements]** Anonymous-block selection endpoints store parent id plus sibling index because anonymous ids change across reconstruction (packages/blitz-dom/src/selection.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/selection.rs:); animations of detached nodes are cleared so an infinite animation cannot force a redraw every frame (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:); pseudo-element style changes needing no reconstruction are flushed during traversal (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:)

- **[Layout]** HTML tables are laid out by Taffy's grid; replaced elements are `img`, `svg`, `canvas`, `video`, `embed` and `iframe`, `<object>` excluded; text nodes are never laid out individually; text, checkbox, radio and range inputs get their control data at construction; damage bits over Servo's `RestyleDamage` decide relayout and reconstruction; only non-zero z-index stacking contexts are hoisted.

- **[Inline SVG]** Inline `<svg>` is re-parsed from its outer HTML into an image and rebuilt when its subtree's style changes (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/inline_svg_serialize.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/inline_svg_restyle.rs:), serialized with `currentColor` resolved and `xmlns:xlink` added (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/serialize.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/serialize.rs:), while `outer_html` does not resolve `currentColor` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/inline_svg_serialize.rs:); SVG `width`/`height` are presentation attributes at the lowest cascade level (tests/blitz-tests/tests/svg_attr_sizing.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/svg_attr_sizing.rs:)

- **[DOM semantics]** `lang`/`xml:lang` and `dir` set language and direction; `disabled` is read by its presence on a form control through one reading — focusability, the pointer and click gates and the Enter and Space activation read it — and an option's through `option_disabled`, its own attribute or its group's; a node the Dioxus bridge removes is dropped with its descendants and no longer resolves; interaction state on removed nodes is cleared or retargeted.

- `inert` is honoured by its presence on the element or an ancestor — not focusable, not hit, out of the accessibility tree and the snapshot; focus keeps `:focus-within` on its ancestors; a `select`'s choice, or a `multiple` select's chosen set, is held as its options' `CHECKED` state, a single select's settled by HTML's selectedness algorithm; its options include its `optgroup` children's; and a controlled app writes `selected` from its `input` event's value or a choice reverts.

- The focus fixup: a node that holds focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives it up at the mutator's flush through `BaseDocument::clear_focus`, with no DOM `blur` or `focusout`; the fixup reads neither `disabled` nor `hidden`.

- **[HTML parsing]** html5ever runs with scripting off, the doctype dropped and no-quirks mode; XHTML is sniffed and parsed as XML; `HtmlDocument` uses the configured `ua_stylesheets` as given; `<template>` children parse into a detached fragment; file input, custom widgets, svg and scrollbar thumb hit-testing are feature-gated.

- **[Networking]** Every request carries a fixed Firefox-on-Linux `User-Agent` (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; examples/screenshot.rs:; examples/screenshot.rs:; examples/paint_bench.rs:; examples/paint_bench.rs:); in-flight requests capped per host by a tokio `Semaphore` of 6 (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:); with `cache` the client uses reqwest-middleware with `http_cache_reqwest::Cache`, `CacheMode::Default`, `CACacheManager`, `shared: false` (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:); `data:` decoded locally, `file:` read from disk, every other scheme HTTP (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:)

- **[Shell and windowing]** windows are created invisible and shown after AccessKit initialises; the renderer is suspended before its window drops, and windows are dropped before the event loop exits; the default event loop waits; iOS redraws, wasm32 resizes and macOS safe areas are handled in the shell; winit's IME event is copied so lower-level Blitz crates do not depend on winit; accesskit_xplat forbids neither or both of `async-io` and `tokio` on Unix.

- **[Painting]** layers are capped at 1024, non-finite transformed boxes culled and gradient layers needing more than 500 tiles not painted; a password input paints masked in every document, a direct engine change whose merge surface is `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs` and `packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs`.

- **[JavaScript]** classic external scripts are fetched synchronously, in document order; Boa's timers are replaced by timers tied to the document event loop; `annex-b` is enabled; DOM wrappers are cached per node, preserving `===` identity; all elements share one prototype; `window.history` is in-memory with no `popstate`; a single frame only.

- **[Node identity]** `NodeId` packs a 32-bit slot index and 32-bit version (packages/blitz-traits/src/node_id.rs:), ordered by index then version to roughly match creation order (packages/blitz-traits/src/node_id.rs:)

- **[Dioxus integration]** `DioxusDocument` defaults its `base_url` to `dioxus://index.html` and adds no stylesheet of its own, the default user-agent sheet reaching it once through `DocumentConfig::default()` and a config that sets `ua_stylesheets` used as given; hot reload only under `hot-reload` with `debug_assertions` off wasm32; in-memory `MemoryHistory` navigation; JS `eval` delegated to `NoOpDocument`; custom content as an `object` whose `data` carries a `CustomWidgetAttr`.

- **[Browser app]** history persists to `history.sqlite3` in the project data dir, in memory where that fails and always on Android and iOS, migrations append-only, at most 1000 entries; disk writes go through tokio `spawn_blocking`; non-URL input becomes a DuckDuckGo search; about pages are Dioxus components; at least one tab is always open.

- **[WPT runner]** an 800x600 render target at scale 1.0; suites default to css-flexbox and css-grid, `full` running every top-level directory but `encoding`; blocked, quarantined, non-UTF-8, testdriver and worker-only tests are skipped; a test's kind decides its runner, under fixed timer budgets; a reftest passes on any match and no mismatch, fuzzy matching allowed.

- **[Driver session]** a session crosses processes on a `std`-only Unix-domain socket in an owner-only state directory and on the `mcp` role's stdio — no third-party IPC crate and no TCP or UDP port; ids, names, masked values, snapshot text, diffs, shots and lint findings cross, never a `NodeId`; the library depends on no app, emits no event, installs no subscriber and reads no env var; a hosted session expires when idle; a new carrier or exit widens the boundary.

- A session whose launcher names a recording directory keeps its answered calls at rest as one owner-only replayable check, never logged and never named by a tool call; the repository's two committed stand checks are the one exception to owner-only.

title: Conventions

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/conventions.md — read whole.

- **Formatting and lints:** `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings`, then upstream's blitz-dom clippy line only when that is green, each a `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh` leg in CI and on the dev host; rustdoc warnings are errors workflow-wide, over every library crate; `collapsible_if` allowed crate-wide in four crates and `module_inception` in blitz-dom's node module, the rest locally, `clippy::expect_used` / `clippy::unwrap_used` next to a justification.

- **Manifests:** dependencies declared once in `[workspace.dependencies]` and consumed as `{ workspace = true }`; in-repo crates declared with `default-features = false`, except the `seven_guis` path entry, which keeps its renderer feature; package metadata inherited with `*.workspace = true`; example and app crates set `publish = false`.

- **Licensing exceptions:** `wasm_hello` takes its licence from the workspace, `license.workspace = true` (examples/wasm_hello/Cargo.toml:); `wgpu_texture` declares `license = "MIT"` with a SixtyFPS header (examples/wgpu_texture/Cargo.toml:; examples/wgpu_texture/src/demo_renderer.rs:); `accesskit_xplat` declares `license = "Apache-2.0"` with AccessKit Authors headers (packages/accesskit_xplat/Cargo.toml:; packages/accesskit_xplat/src/lib.rs:); blitz-dom's `assets/default.css` carries an MPL 2.0 header (packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css:); `stylo_taffy` declares `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR MPL-2.0"` — the workspace's dual licence plus MPL 2.0 (packages/stylo_taffy/Cargo.toml:)

- **Documentation:** modules and files open with `//!` docs, public items carry `///`, spec URLs are cited above or next to implementations, doc comments state the rationale for constants, and examples open with a `//!` comment describing what they demonstrate.
- **Known gaps:** marked with `TODO`/`FIXME`; an ordering-sensitive block is marked "WARNING: DO NOT REORDER"; sections delimited with `// === … ===`.

- **Visibility and naming:** crate internals are `pub(crate)` / `pub(super)`; no-op implementations are prefixed `Dummy` and internal JS natives `__blitz_`; consuming builder methods `with_…` / `without_…`; `#[non_exhaustive]` on `NavigationOptions` and `Request`; Stylo and Parley types aliased under `stylo` / `parley` modules; paint rendering split one module per concern.

- **Feature gating:** optional functionality gated by cargo features; in the engine and upstream crates tracing is gated per call site with a `cfg(not(feature = "tracing"))` fallback, while escher's own two crates take `tracing` ungated — escher-telemetry emits its startup and panic events ungated and escher-driver builds its spans by hand, with no `#[instrument]`; desktop-only code gated by a repeated cfg list.

- **Unsafe and borrowing:** `unsafe` blocks carry `allow unsafe_code` or `// SAFETY:` comments; borrow conflicts worked around by taking a child list or layout out and restoring it; let-chains in `if` conditions; a macro generates forwarding accessors for `ElementData`/`DocumentData` fields.

- **Error handling:** error types are enums with `Display` and `From` per wrapped error (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:); mutex locks recover from poisoning with `unwrap_or_else(|err| err.into_inner())` (wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:; wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:; wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:); examples fail with `.unwrap()`, `.expect(..)`, `panic!` (examples/inner_html.rs:; examples/inner_html.rs:; examples/screenshot.rs:; examples/preact_script.rs:)

- **DOM API patterns:** mutations go through `DocumentMutator`, which flushes deferred work on `Drop` and requests a redraw only for in-document mutations (packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:); `DocumentMutator::doc` is a public escape hatch with a request to prefer extending the mutator (packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:); a Stylo snapshot is taken before attribute mutation of in-document nodes (packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); event-producing functions take a `dispatch_event` callback (packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/events/focus.rs:); repeated regexes held in `LazyLock<Regex>` or compiled per worker (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/fuzzy.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/mod.rs:; wpt/runner/src/main.rs:)

- **Tests:** unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of the source file, or in a `#[path]` child file of their own; each integration test file covers one behavior and opens with a `//!` doc naming it; scenarios run in both layout modes; stand checks share helpers through modules under `tests/` that are no test target; tests first assert the fixture produces the condition; blitz-tests keeps one test target per file, except upstream's `tests/all.rs`, declared and held at `test = false`.

- Unit-test modules moved to files of their own keep their test paths; `tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs` states the fixture boot and hold, the shared fixture pages and `HeldNet` once, and a page with one reader stays in its check's file.

- **Apps and examples:** binaries set `windows_subsystem = "windows"` outside tests; Android entry points are `android_main` calling `set_android_app`; reactive state uses `#[derive(Store)]`; assets come through `asset!`; Dioxus examples declare `dioxus_native::launch(app)` with `#[component]` components and signal and store hooks, their CSS in `const` raw strings.

- **HTML fixtures:** reduced variants sit beside full pages; feature fixtures group numbered cases under h2/h3 headings with a CSS comment per case; sibling assets referenced with `./`-relative URLs; graphite.html is minified, and some captures stand as captured, without a closing head, body or html tag or a doctype.

title: Standard Contracts

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/standard-contracts.md — read whole.

- **Document core (blitz-dom):** the `Document` trait every document wrapper implements; `DocumentConfig` carrying the viewport, providers, user-agent sheets, fonts, media type, threading, incremental flag, abort signal, depth and clock; resource loading; the changed set read by `has_changes` and drained by `take_changed_nodes`, its ids read through `get_node`, never by indexing; the read-only `can_paint_text` and `layout_as_text_input`.

- The document's clock: `DocumentConfig.clock`, the config's clock or else a fresh `WallClock`; the crate root re-exports `Clock`, `WallClock` and `VirtualClock`, every clone of a `VirtualClock` reading one time; no `Instant::now()` or `SystemTime::now()` stands in blitz-dom outside `clock.rs`; `BaseDocument::select_value` reads a select's value, a `multiple` select's first chosen option in tree order, `select_values` its chosen set and `select_of` an option's or group's select, each public and read-only; public `clear_select_typeahead` clears the typed text, its one non-test caller the driver's `focus_select`; the choice's writers are crate-private.

- An open select's list on `BaseDocument`: `open_select`, `select_list_bounds`, `select_list_view` and `select_row_layout` are public and read-only; public `close_select_list` closes an open list, its callers keyboard, pointer, reconcile and the driver's `focus_select`; the rest of the list's machinery is crate-private or private.

- **Mutation, query and CSSOM:** mutations through `doc.mutate()`; selector queries returning `Result`, never matching the scope node; CSSOM by owner `NodeId` and an index path; `build_accessibility_tree` returns an AccessKit `TreeUpdate`, naming nodes from text children, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, a bound `<label>` and option and group labels, and writing state attributes each read once, a native control's checked state on a checkable role and a single select's native `expanded`, true while its list stands open, with no `aria-expanded` read on one, every other element keeping that read; blitz-shell refreshes the platform tree when a poll took a non-empty changed set.

- A native control under a role that is not checkable writes no checked state, and neither author attribute is read on one; a measured limit: the platform-tree refresh's windowed witness is still owed, the refresh held by the document-level tests and both feature builds of blitz-shell.

- **Events:** `EventHandler` and `EventDriver` dispatch DOM events — mouse compatibility and touch events from pointers, non-bubbling events to the target only, a focus change as `blur`, `focusout`, `focus`, `focusin`, but for the focus fixup under `inert`, which clears focus and dispatches none of them, and for the driver's `type` on any select, which focuses with no click and dispatches none of them either; a range input's default actions dispatch `input`; Enter and a released Space dispatch a Click the driver queues, so the app's handlers run before the default action; the engine dispatches `change` after `input` on a select's choice and on a checkbox's or radio's click, a radio only where it was not checked before, and a page's script hears that one `change`; a text or range input's `input` brings none.

- **Scrolling, selection, tree:** the `BaseDocument` scroll API; `scroll_into_view` scrolls every scrolling box on the target's chain, nested ones instantly with no `scroll` event, then the viewport, but for a row of an open select list, which writes the list's `scroll_y` at once and moves no chain or viewport; `visible_region` is the read-only reader of what can be seen, and seeing is never read from a hit; a hit stops at the padding box of a box paint clips, skips a node dropped since the last resolve, and answers nothing for the whole subtree of a transform whose determinant is 0 or not finite, while `hit_with_scrollbar` answers an open select list first and no scrollbar with it, `hit_inner` holding none of it, so `hit`, `set_hover_to` and `handle_pointerdown` all read the list; `Node::absolute_position` subtracts only ancestors' scroll offsets; stale-id `NodeTree` indexing panics.

- `get_client_bounding_rect` reads an element where its transforms move it, and `visible_region` reads each clipping box through its transforms, exact under a translate and a scale and under a rotation the rotated padding box's bounding box, so it holds corners the box does not show (a measured limit), a mapped box with a non-finite edge answering `None`, and a row or a group of an open select list reading the list's scrollport in place of its clipping boxes; `BaseDocument::text_extent` is a read-only reader that mutates nothing.

- **Layout:** the crate-private `LayoutPassState` implements Taffy's traversal and layout traits for one pass — `BaseDocument` implements none; the table, replaced-element and paint-tree APIs; `stylo_taffy` exports `to_taffy_style`, `TaffyStyloStyle`, `StyleFlags`, `Atom`, `WritingMode` and `WritingModeExt`.

- **Nodes and widgets:** `NodeData` and `SpecialElementData` (not `#[non_exhaustive]`, `RangeInput` among its variants); `RangeInputData` read through the `ElementData` range accessors; serialization and CSSOM View accessors; the `Widget` trait, a widget's resources unregistered when its node drops.

- `ElementData::is_disabled` is the one disabled reading of a form control — a `disabled` attribute present; an option's is the one rule `option_disabled`, its own attribute or its group's; the select's rules live in the crate-private `node::select`, with no public type; an open list's state lives in `node::select_list`, crate-private but for two public read types re-exported from the crate root, `SelectListView`, the list's colours its associated constants, and `SelectListRow`.

- **Provider traits (blitz-traits):** `NetProvider` (a no-op one registering no pending-critical resources), `NetHandler`, `NetWaker`, `Request`, `Body`, `FormData`, `AbortController`/`AbortSignal`, `NavigationProvider`, `ShellProvider` with no-op defaults, `HtmlParserProvider`, `DevtoolSettings` and `Viewport`, its `scale()` hidpi_scale × zoom.

- **HTML and networking crates:** blitz-html's `HtmlDocument`, `DocumentHtmlParser` (an html5ever `TreeSink`) and `HtmlProvider`; blitz-net's `Provider` implementing `NetProvider::fetch`, with typed `ProviderError`s and byte, form or empty request bodies.

- **Paint and shell:** `paint_scene` paints a document into a `PaintScene`, an open select's list last through `paint_select_list`, after the root's render and before the devtools overlays, read from `SelectListView` and past any clip or `opacity` on its select's ancestors, reaching a shell or renderer through `paint_scene` alone; blitz-shell's application, proxy, view, window config and shell provider, the embedder completing a resume; a password `input` paints its value masked in every document and through every renderer that paints with blitz-paint, its caret placed by the bullets, so no width of the real characters reaches a frame or the caret.

- **Test harness:** blitz-test-harness's `Harness`, generic over the document, with constructors, inspection and input helpers that pump and never settle; `screenshot` and `screenshot_rect` paint a raster through blitz-paint, printing, panicking and logging nothing; `text_contrast` reads a WCAG contrast and changes nothing; `settle` drives render and layout to quiet, reports a load in flight and never waits on one or moves time.
- The harness holds one `VirtualClock` its documents share; `tick` and `advance_time` move it, and `screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` and `settle` never do.

- **Headless stand (seven_guis, native only):** `seven_guis::stand` boots the four lean tasks and, beside them, Cells (`boot_cells`, no `LeanTask`) and a load page (`boot_load`) in a pinned 800x600 Light viewport with one bundled font, every boot offline but the load page's, whose one stylesheet fetch the in-process stand-in `LoadNet` answers after `LOAD_ANSWER_DELAY` (200 ms); `timer_step` hands the Timer its ticks for a driver session; it installs no telemetry, reads no env var and names no `blitz_net`.

- **Telemetry bootstrap (escher-telemetry):** `init` installs one stderr sink once, `ForeignSubscriber` (never a panic) when another is global; one line per event and per closed span, stamped `service.name` and `service.version`; a target outside the engine and escher prefix sets is dropped whole at every level, an engine target prints only `SAFE_FIELDS`, `CONTENT_FIELDS` always redacted; the panic hook chains.

- **Driver session (escher-driver):** a `Session` (one booted app) runs every call through `Session::run`, which validates first; nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`; the command and refusal schema stated once as `'static` data — twelve verbs, eight closed causes, no refusal holding what a call supplied; the `v3` wire, the command line, the MCP server and the `command` and `tool_call` spans carry it; no `NodeId` crosses, and nothing logs an id, a name or a value.

- Every answer is written by hand in the crate-private `json` module — no serialization crate writes one, `serde_json` only reading MCP requests and kept checks — and no command's ending writes back anything the caller typed.

- The recording keeps a session's answered calls as a kept check, a masked `type` as its stand-in and a shot without its pixels; `Check::replay` runs them again through `Session::run`; `Session::lint` reads the screen and changes nothing; `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s) bounds an acting step's wait for a load, moving no time.

- **JavaScript (blitz-vibey-script):** `ScriptFetcher` and the `ScriptDocument` API run a document's scripts on Boa, JS listeners before Blitz default actions; the public `document_may_load` lets a `file:` URL load only for a `file:` document, its refusal a `FetchError` variant, checked by `fetch()`, a module `import` and `<script src>`; `__blitz_` globals carry messages and synchronous fetches, and `__blitz_parse_search_params`, the bootstrap's own, is deleted from `globalThis` before any page script; a JS bootstrap defines history, fetch, DOMException, the CSSOM classes and `URLSearchParams` with `URL.prototype.searchParams`, `href` and `search` live both ways; escher uses none of the script text-selection and `innerText` readers.

- **High-level launch:** blitz's `launch_url` and `launch_static_html`; dioxus-native's `launch`, `launch_cfg` and `launch_cfg_with_props`, configs downcast and unmatched ones dropped; the `Config` builders, the window hooks and the native head-element events.

- **Dioxus DOM bridge:** DOM events reach the vdom through `data-dioxus-id`; a falsy value of upstream's 28 boolean attributes clears the attribute; `DioxusDocument::element_id` and `element_ids` compute a stable id on demand in four tiers — author key, anchored path, component path, document path — written to neither DOM nor vdom; under `accessibility` the snapshot, its text form and its diff read the screen read-only, holding no `NodeId`.
- No log or event carries the snapshot, its text or a diff, except a diff's three counts — added, removed and changed — on escher-driver's command span.
- Every element an agent can act on reads an author key: `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` lists, read-only, each actionable element whose stable id holds a `/`, with a remedy naming the fix.

- `is_masked_input` is the one masked-control test, a password or file `input`; the public `closed_select_of`, which answers `None` for a select whose list is open, and `is_select`, read by the driver's `locate` alone, are the select tests the driver reads, naming the element and never the role, and `is_multiple_select` stays re-exported, read within the workspace by `closed_select_of` alone; a select's `input` and `change` reach the app as form data, a `multiple` select's as one `(name, FormValue::Text(value))` per chosen option, so `evt.values()` reads the set and `value` stays `select_value`; its options are its children in the snapshot, a `multiple` select's rows and groups reading client rects of their own and an open list's rows and groups reading `select_list_bounds` before the client rect.

- **Accessibility adapter:** `accesskit_xplat` `WindowEvent` (InitialTreeRequested, ActionRequested, AccessibilityDeactivated), `EventHandler`, `Adapter` with `with_split_handlers`, `with_combined_handler`, `update_if_active`, `set_focus`, `set_window_bounds` (packages/accesskit_xplat/src/lib.rs:); each platform adapter exposes `new`, `update_if_active`, `set_focus`, `set_window_bounds` (packages/accesskit_xplat/src/platform_impl/null.rs:; packages/accesskit_xplat/src/platform_impl/unix.rs:)

- **CLIs:** the command lines of the examples and apps (`paint_bench`, `screenshot`, `preact_script`, `multi_doc`, browser, rdme, wgpu_texture, wpt), and `escher-session <verb> [arguments] --session <dir>`, the driver's command line over six served stand tasks — the four lean ones, Cells and the load page, its usage line's apps and the MCP `start` tool's `enum` written from one private table —, with its `serve` host role and its `mcp` role, answering one line of JSON and exiting `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error.

- **Browser app:** the history store and its `history_entries` table, the browser's navigation provider, document loader and config, the about URLs, View Source and the URL suggester; rdme's navigation provider and events.

- **WPT runner outputs:** an `output` directory recreated each run, holding `wpt_expectations.txt`, `wptreport.json` and the reftest images; the harness and subtest codes, the result line, kinds, statuses and flags; the runner's script fetcher and net provider.

- **CI contracts:** `wpt_diff_to_pr.py` writes WPT results into a PR body; the WPT results dispatch runs only on `DioxusLabs/blitz`; `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh {leg}` is the one leg runner of CI and the dev host; `apt-install.sh` the one bounded, retried package install; `coverage_floor.py` the per-crate coverage floor; `scripts/agent-run.sh` and `scripts/cold-agent.sh` the agent-run test and cold-agent pipe contracts, in full in test-plan §3.

- **Fixture forms:** the google fixture's search form GETs `/search` with a textarea `q` (maxlength 2048), submit inputs `btnK`/`btnI` and hidden inputs `sca_esv`, `source`, `ei`, `iflsig` (examples/assets/google.html:; examples/assets/google.html:; examples/assets/google.html:; examples/assets/google.html:; examples/assets/google.html:); the graphite fixture's newsletter form POSTs to `https://graphite.art/newsletter-signup` with name, phone, email (examples/assets/graphite.html:)

title: Occupied Resources

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/occupied-resources.md — read whole.

- **Network ports and listeners:** no served network port, TCP or UDP, blitz-net's tests alone binding TCP on loopback, served by no binary and reached by no caller, so no crossing; one local listener, the driver session's Unix-domain socket `{state_dir}/session.sock` (`0600`, in a `0700` state directory), unix only; the `escher-session mcp` role speaks over its own stdio, with no listener; still no second served listener.

- **Outbound hosts:** the WPT report on GitHub Pages (an upstream-only job), DuckDuckGo search, the examples' default sites, test base URLs, WPT's `http://dummy.local`, and the model provider, reached by the spawned `claude` client on the operator-driven live cold-agent run only — never in CI, and no escher code makes the request.

- **URL schemes and identities:** `dioxus` scheme default base `dioxus://index.html`, served from the file system by `dioxus_asset_resolver::native::serve_asset` (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:; packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:); `navigator.userAgent` `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Blitz)` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/bootstrap.rs:); `location` without base URL is `about:blank`, origin `null` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/window.rs:); bundle identifier `com.dioxuslabs.blitz` (apps/browser/Dioxus.toml:); default window title the dioxus-cli-config app title, else "Dioxus App" (packages/dioxus-native/src/config.rs:); app root `<main id="main">` under `<body>` (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:); WASM canvas id `blitz-target` (examples/wasm_hello/index.html:; examples/wasm_hello/src/lib.rs:); Windows icon resource id 32512 (apps/browser/src/main.rs:)

- **Filesystem:** the browser's history database and HTTP cache, screenshot and example outputs, WPT's `output`, CI leg logs under `target/ci-logs/`, the coverage report, the agent-run and cold-agent state areas under `target/`, local only and uploaded by no CI job, and the driver session's state directory — a path its caller names, never an env read or a default, created `0700`, holding `session.sock` alone, removed at stop or idle expiry.

- The recording directory is a path the launcher names by `--record <dir>`, never an env read or a default and named by no tool call, created `0700` and refused when open to its group or others; escher removes a check only when its recording ends on a failed write or a passed bound, never a file it did not create and never the directory; the two committed checks under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/` are the one exception to a kept check's owner-only medium.

- **Process-wide state and threads:** Stylo's global rayon pool, its `Parallel` traversals serialised by the static `PARALLEL_TRAVERSAL_LOCK`, static id counters, a thread-local layout context, the script timer thread and the stand load page's network stand-in `LoadNet`, one thread per fetch; mimalloc the global allocator of the browser app (by default) and the WPT runner; escher-telemetry's global subscriber, `log` bridge and chaining panic hook in both seven_guis binaries, spawning no thread; the `escher-session` host one process with one session and one listener, its `mcp` role at most one session in process; test binaries re-executing themselves with a fixed argv, two as a session host on its Unix-domain socket.

- **System services:** clipboard written through the shell provider on copy (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:); native file dialog through the shell provider (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:)
- **Keyboard shortcuts:** Ctrl or Meta with Equal, Minus, Digit0 for zoom; Alt with D toggles layout display, H hover highlight, T prints the taffy tree (packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:)

- **Environment variables:** `RUST_LOG`, the filter `escher_telemetry::init` reads, `warn` when unset or unparsable; `WPT_DIR`; `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML`; `MULTI_DOC_N`, `MULTI_DOC_SEQ` and `MULTI_DOC_FLAT`, read by the `multi_doc` example alone; `TMPDIR`, at two test-only sites (escher-driver's client unit test and blitz-vibey-script's `tests/dom.rs`); the CI script's GitHub variables.

- **Names:** the workspace's crates, among them escher-telemetry and escher-driver, `publish = false` libraries; binaries `blitz`, `seven_guis_native`, `escher-session` and `todomvc_native`; crate features; the scripts `scripts/cold-agent.sh` and `scripts/cold-agent.ps1`; the MCP server name `escher`, allowed as `mcp__escher`.

- **CI infrastructure:** the "Signed Builds" and "WPT" environments and the WPT runner label, reached only from `DioxusLabs/blitz`; the fork's GitHub Actions cache, with a 10 GB per-repository budget, least-recently-used eviction, the test job saving `workspace-test`, which `a11y` and `stand-repeat` restore with `save-if: false`.

title: Infrastructure Patterns

body: - **Build system:** Cargo workspace with shared `[workspace.dependencies]` (Cargo.toml:; Cargo.toml:); fmt and clippy gates, a workflow-wide rustdoc `-D warnings` setting the docs job enforces over every workspace library crate, and a cargo-deny advisory gate configured by the root `deny.toml` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:; .github/workflows/ci.yml:; .github/workflows/ci.yml:; .github/workflows/ci.yml:; deny.toml:); Nix flake exposing `packages.browser` (binary `blitz`) as default and a `blitz-dev` devShell (flake.nix:), wrapping Linux packages with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for dlopen'd wayland, libxkbcommon, libGL, vulkan-loader and X11 libs (flake.nix:; flake.nix:); `Cross.toml` pre-build adds `$CROSS_DEB_ARCH` and installs `python3` (Cross.toml:); blitz-dom depends on objc2 with `disable-encoding-assertions` on Apple targets, a HACK to stop debug builds panicking (packages/blitz-dom/Cargo.toml:); a default user-agent stylesheet and bullet font are embedded at compile time (packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:)
- **Directory structure** (Cargo.toml:; Cargo.toml:; Cargo.toml:):

```
Cargo.toml             workspace root + virtual package (examples/*.rs via `cargo run --example`)
.config/nextest.toml   cargo-nextest profiles — one, `mutants`, the mutation tier's; the default profile untouched
packages/
  accesskit_xplat  debug_timer  blitz-traits  blitz-dom  blitz-html  blitz-net
  blitz-paint  blitz-vibey-script  blitz-shell  blitz  stylo_taffy
  dioxus-native  dioxus-native-dom  blitz-test-harness  escher-telemetry
  escher-driver
apps/
  browser/  browser/persistence/  readme/
wpt/runner/
tests/blitz-tests/     checks/ — the two committed kept checks `stand_replay` replays
examples/
  counter/  transparent/  seven_guis/  todomvc/  wgpu_texture/  wasm_hello/
scripts/               agent-run.{sh,ps1} (test contract) · cold-agent.{sh,ps1} (cold-agent pipe) · code-graph tooling
docs/                  capabilities.md (escher's capability statement) beside upstream's three files — an upstream change under docs/ never conflicts with it
sites/                 excluded from the workspace
```

- **Deployment model:** desktop/mobile bundles of the browser through `dx bundle --package browser --release --profile production --locked` (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:), built only on `DioxusLabs/blitz` — the `release-cli` job carries `if: github.repository == 'DioxusLabs/blitz'`, so the fork builds no bundle and never enters "Signed Builds"; its ref-keyed `environment:` and step `if:` expressions stand but are unreachable there (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:) — over Windows x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/aarch64, Linux x86_64/aarch64, Android aarch64 (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:), uploaded unzipped with `actions/upload-artifact@v7` (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:), `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: 2` "to debug possible OOM" (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:); Windows bundle `webview_install_mode = "Skip"` (apps/browser/Dioxus.toml:) with bundle publisher DioxusLabs (apps/browser/Dioxus.toml:); WASM entry points use `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]`, `console_error_panic_hook` and bundled DejaVuSans.woff2 — seven_guis' bytes are the crate-root `DEJAVU_SANS`, compiled on native too, where the headless stand registers the same font (examples/seven_guis/src/lib.rs:; examples/todomvc/src/wasm.rs:; examples/wasm_hello/src/lib.rs:; examples/wasm_hello/src/lib.rs:); Android Activities locate the native view and request focus (apps/browser/MainActivity.kt:; examples/todomvc/MainActivity.kt:)

- **Runtime threading and event flow:** each document owns an mpsc channel drained by `handle_messages` at the start of `resolve` (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:); fetches go through `NetProvider::fetch` with a `ResourceHandler` that sends on the channel then `request_redraw` (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:), stamped with the document's `AbortSignal` (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/config.rs:); a failed fetch reaches the handler through `NetHandler::error`, a public default that does nothing, blitz-net's error arm calling it before the waker, and `ResourceHandler<StylesheetHandler>::error` responds `Err`, so the request leaves `pending_critical_resources` and a failed, empty or non-CSS stylesheet stops blocking render (packages/blitz-traits/src/net.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:); iframe loads use a per-iframe `AbortController` generation (packages/blitz-dom/src/iframe.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/iframe.rs:) and inherit the parent's providers and settings (packages/blitz-dom/src/iframe.rs:); device changes are coalesced into one rebuild at the next resolve (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); `resolve` order: messages, critical-resource gate, scroll animation, device changes, stylist, damage propagation, layout-children construction, deferred tasks, style images, layout, transforms, paint tree, clear damage, `reconcile_select_list`, hover refresh, sub-documents (packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:); under `parallel-construct` inline-layout tasks run on rayon with thread-local font contexts (packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); layout cached per node through Taffy's `CacheTree` (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:), the out-of-flow pass inside the cache wrapper (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:); style images fetched via `net_provider.fetch` with `image_cache` and `pending_images` (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs:); the font context shared behind a lock (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/list.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:);
 hoisted positions and stacking-context bounds memoised in `Cell`s by geometry generation (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/paint_tree.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/paint_tree.rs:); fetches spawned with `tokio::spawn` natively and `wasm_bindgen_futures::spawn_local` on wasm32 (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:), abortable via an `AbortFetch` wrapper (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:), a `DummyNetWaker` without a waker (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:) and `Provider::count` as the waker `Arc`'s strong count minus one (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:); target-specific dependency sets for Android and wasm32 (packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml:)

- **Shell loop:** shell events flow through an mpsc channel drained in `proxy_wake_up` (packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/event.rs:); every window event is followed by a Poll (packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:); a futures waker sends Poll events (packages/blitz-shell/src/event.rs:); renderer resume inline on native, a spawned future on wasm32 (packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:); on wasm32 a 0x0 surface seeds the viewport from the canvas's CSS box (packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:); custom widgets pre-painted into Scenes keyed by document and node id (packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs:); docs.rs builds with all features (packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:)

- **Launch paths:** blitz builds a default event loop, `BlitzShellProxy`, `BlitzApplication`, one window, and runs (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:), entering a tokio multi-thread runtime with `net` off wasm32 (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:); net provider `blitz_net::Provider` with `net`, else `DummyNetProvider` (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:), whose non-`net` branch references `event_loop`, which is not a parameter of that function (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:); dioxus-native creates the event loop and runs `run_app` (packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:; packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:), enters a tokio runtime with `net` off wasm32 (packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:), creates a `blitz_net::Provider` with the shell proxy as waker wrapped by `DioxusNativeNetProvider` (packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:), else a data-URI provider or none (packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:); hot reload via `dioxus_devtools::connect` (packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:), applying vdom changes and reloading assets, a devserver `Shutdown` exiting the loop (packages/dioxus-native/src/dioxus_application.rs:); `DioxusNativeApplication` delegates to an inner `BlitzApplication` (packages/dioxus-native/src/dioxus_application.rs:); Android `set_android_app`/`current_android_app` (packages/dioxus-native/src/lib.rs:); wasm32 default window appends a canvas to the body (packages/dioxus-native/src/config.rs:); macOS handler extension forwarded (packages/dioxus-native/src/dioxus_application.rs:; packages/dioxus-native/src/dioxus_application.rs:); rdme and `restyle` build and enter a tokio multi-thread runtime before the event loop (apps/readme/src/main.rs:; apps/readme/Cargo.toml:; examples/restyle.rs:)

- **JavaScript runtime:** a background thread sleeps until the next JS timer deadline and wakes the event loop, respawned when its channel disconnects (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:); each JS entry point requests a redraw and re-arms the timer thread (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:); the ES module loader fetches through the ScriptFetcher, gated by `document_may_load`, and caches modules by URL (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/modules.rs:); interval timers reschedule at least 1ms, due timers soonest-first (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/timers.rs:)

title: Cross-cutting Patterns

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/cross-cutting-patterns.md — read whole.
- **Development Style signal:** agent-driven

- **Config management:** documents configured through `DocumentConfig`; optional capabilities are compile-time Cargo features forwarded down the crates, `accessibility` also gating the dioxus-native-dom snapshot modules; launch configs downcast at launch; platform behaviour gated by `cfg(target_os = ...)` and `IS_MOBILE`; runtime inputs are CLI arguments and environment variables.

- **Logging and timing:** escher binaries install `escher_telemetry::init` at start — a stderr-only sink stamping the service identity, bridging `log`, dropping every record outside the engine and escher prefix sets at every level whatever `RUST_LOG` names, scrubbing what prints and chaining the panic hook; escher-driver emits its spans ungated and installs no subscriber; the upstream `fmt::init()` installs run only under `tracing` and write stdout unscrubbed.

- **Error handling:** fallible APIs return typed results — `Result<_, CssomError>` (packages/blitz-dom/src/cssom.rs:), `Result<_, ParseError>` (packages/blitz-dom/src/query_selector.rs:), `Result<Resource, String>` (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:); uncaught JS errors go through `report_js_error`, firing a window `error` event with a re-dispatch guard (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/events.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/state.rs:), capped at 256 between drains (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/state.rs:); DOMException errors built through the bootstrap's global, falling back to TypeError (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/mod.rs:); WPT drains JS errors and logs them with `warn!` (wpt/runner/src/test_runners/attr_test.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/ref_test.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/harness_test.rs:)

- **Service wiring:** shell and navigation providers carry redraw, clipboard, file dialogs and link navigation; redraws are requested after mutations, loads, hover, device changes and a focus set or cleared, and skipped while critical resources are pending or the window is occluded; Dioxus services are root contexts; shared state is `Rc<RefCell<…>>`.

- **Event processing:** default-action events are queued and processed in order, handlers before the default action unless cancelled; sub-document and custom-widget events forwarded with adjusted coordinates; Dioxus skips event kinds with zero handlers; JS microtasks drained after eval, timers and dispatch; style and layout resolved before JS geometry reads; shortcuts use Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere.

- **Invalidation and state integrity:** interaction state on a removed node is cleared or retargeted before the node is freed; damage propagates up the DOM and to anonymous ancestors and is cleared in one visit; geometry memoisation is invalidated by a generation counter; the changed set is written at five kinds of site, the fifth a select list's open and close marking its select, and, with no list open, by no node creation, hover, scroll, resize, load, animation or layout; where a list stands, a page scroll or a move that closes it marks its select through `reconcile_select_list` at the next resolve and a wheel elsewhere through `close_select_list`, while a highlight or a wheel move inside the list marks nothing; the shell rebuilds the platform tree only when a poll took a non-empty set.

- **Rendering details:** legacy presentational attributes map to CSS at the presentational-hints level (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:); `display: contents` handled by hoisting children into the nearest non-contents container (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:); viewport scale applied to Parley measurements and divided back out (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/inline/layout.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/inline/layout.rs:)

- **Unsafe aliasing:** `Node` holds a raw `*mut NodeTree` commented "This is unsafe!!" with `unsafe impl Send` and `Sync` (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:)

- **WPT bucketing:** feature-usage flags are computed by regex over test sources to bucket failures (wpt/runner/src/test_runners/mod.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/ref_test.rs:; wpt/runner/src/main.rs:)

title: Project Intent

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/project-intent.md — read whole.
Origin: adopted at 0f60502ea724ef703b34220b3847bb3483f70b5f

Upstream sync: DioxusLabs/blitz `main` last merged at 23b9b26a9b6af5947b8f003d2c2cc768bff10b8a — the next sync's merge base; upstream `main` last read at `e42ee1f25`, thirty-six of the fifty-seven commits past the merge base taken by no-commit cherry-picks with the merge base unmoved and twenty-one left out (as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph/evidence/lock.md); git Stylo 0.23-pre, the six Taffy-main commits and Dioxus 0.8.0-alpha.3 wait for escher's next version, so Stylo stays "0.22.0", Taffy the registry "0.15" and Dioxus "0.7.3".

escher is a fork of Blitz being turned into an agent-first UI framework — a headless driver (CLI + MCP), stable ids for every element, a compact semantic snapshot of the screen, proven on an internal 7GUIs stand. Development Style agent-driven is the founder's word: the framework's own driver is meant to become the harness.

- **Product type:** a Rust library workspace for an HTML/CSS engine — high-level APIs for rendering HTML with Blitz, the core DOM abstraction with `BaseDocument` its primary entry point, the `Document` trait letting blitz-shell drive every wrapper around it; homepage and repository `https://github.com/Turbolet85/escher`.

- **Front page:** the root `README.md` is escher's own page, not upstream Blitz's — what escher is, its status, how the driver's command line and MCP surface are run, its Blitz lineage, licence and contact, and a link to `docs/capabilities.md`, the statement of what Escher can do and its limits, the name spelled «Escher» in its prose and title, crate, binary and path names, URLs and the e-mail unchanged; no build or doc step reads it, one test does — the capability-statement pin reads its count of the driver commands an MCP client gets as tools — and at an Upstream sync an upstream change to `README.md` resolves to escher's version.

- **Crate purposes:** each crate as its own description states it — blitz-html the HTML parser, blitz-net networking, blitz-paint painting through anyrender, blitz-shell the application shell, blitz-test-harness the headless test harness, blitz-vibey-script JavaScript on Boa, blitz-traits the shared traits, debug_timer timings, blitz-dom the DOM, accesskit_xplat the cross-platform AccessKit adapter, and the Dioxus crates.

- **Apps and demonstrators:** `apps/browser` is "The example browser app", binary `blitz` (flake.nix:); rdme "Markdown renderering app" (apps/readme/Cargo.toml:); seven_guis "Seven benchmark tasks for GUI frameworks" (examples/seven_guis/src/app.rs:); todomvc "The typical TodoMVC app, implemented in Dioxus." (examples/todomvc/src/app.rs:); wgpu_texture shows custom WGPU content beneath and above HTML layers (examples/wgpu_texture/src/html.rs:); an example page shows "the built-in cursor styles supported by blitz" (examples/assets/cursor.html:); the Preact TodoMVC page is the default JavaScript-enabled document (examples/preact_script.rs:; examples/preact/index.html:); the reference page frames its API list as what an engine must provide for Preact, React and the WPT harness (examples/preact/core_dom_apis.html:; examples/preact/core_dom_apis.html:)

- **Embedding targets named in code:** `is_noop` serves integrations feeding a pre-rendered DOM, naming aginxbrowser (packages/blitz-traits/src/net.rs:); `ShellProvider` window chrome controls are for documents that draw their own titlebar (packages/blitz-traits/src/shell.rs:); the in-memory JS history is described as sufficient for SPA routers such as React Router (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/bootstrap/window.js:); `take_messages` is used "by the WPT runner to collect testharness.js results" (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:)

- **Validation sources:** web-platform-tests run by the WPT runner from a local checkout, blitz-tests' integration tests — some of them Rust ports of script-driven WPT tests — and regressions and fixtures traced to real sites and applications.

- **Growth model and how functionality is added (as built):** a Cargo workspace of separately usable member crates (Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:), with optional capabilities added as Cargo features forwarded across crates (packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:; packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml:) and blitz packages versioned together through the workspace version and the in-repo `=` pins (Cargo.toml:; Cargo.toml:)

body: Detail: .andromeda/architecture-detail/inherited-defaults.md — read whole.

- Framework: Rust Cargo workspace, edition "2024", rust-version "1.91.0" (Cargo.toml:; Cargo.toml:; Cargo.toml:); engine crates pinned `=0.3.0-beta.4` (Cargo.toml:); Stylo "0.22.0" (Cargo.toml:), taffy "0.15" from the registry (Cargo.toml:), parley "0.12" from the registry (Cargo.toml:), anyrender "0.14.0" (Cargo.toml:), Dioxus "0.7.3" (Cargo.toml:), winit "=0.31.0-beta.3" (Cargo.toml:)

- Database: SQLite via rusqlite 0.32 (bundled) with rusqlite_migration 1.3 in browser-persistence (apps/browser/persistence/Cargo.toml:), file `history.sqlite3` (apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:)

- API style: native Rust API (packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:) with embedder services as `DocumentConfig` provider traits defaulting to `Dummy*` no-ops (packages/blitz-dom/src/config.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); no served network (TCP or UDP) listener, and one local Unix-domain socket — the driver session's socket, carrying its lifecycle and its calls (see Occupied Resources)

- Deployment: browser bundled per platform with `dx bundle --package browser --release --profile production --locked` (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:) — upstream only: the job is repository-guarded to `DioxusLabs/blitz` and does not run on the escher fork (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:); Nix flake `packages.browser` (flake.nix:); WASM examples via Trunk (examples/wasm_hello/index.html:)
- Development Style: agent-driven

- Publishability: the root package is virtual and not meant to be published; app and example crates, blitz-tests, blitz-test-harness, escher-telemetry, escher-driver, blitz-vibey-script and wpt set `publish = false`, rdme `publish = true`; the published `packages/` library crates are versioned together through the workspace version and the in-repo `=` pins.

- Code quality: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --locked -- -D warnings` and upstream's blitz-dom clippy line, all run through `.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh`; rustdoc `-D warnings` over every workspace library crate; a cargo-deny audit of the whole workspace's advisories and licences, a cargo-llvm-cov coverage report gated by per-crate floors, and the `stand-repeat` leg's zero-failure budget.
- Optional capabilities: Cargo features, tracing gated per call site in the engine crates — escher-telemetry and escher-driver (its `command` and `tool_call` spans) are ungated.

- **Radically modular, embeddable engine** — the engine is a set of separately usable crates around a headless DOM that external code drives and any renderer can paint.
  - The root manifest describes its crate as "Top level crate for Blitz" with keywords dom, ui, gui, react, wasm (Cargo.toml:); a captured GitHub profile fixture shows the repository description "A radically modular HTML/CSS rendering engine" (examples/assets/github_profile_reduced2.html:)
  - The blitz crate describes Blitz as "a modular, embeddable web engine with a native Rust API" that powers the dioxus-native UI framework (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:); it "does not bring any unique functionality" and re-exports the relevant crates as modules, each also usable stand-alone (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:)
  - blitz-dom is a flexible headless DOM (`BaseDocument`) designed to be embedded in and "driven" by external code, with most users expected to use a wrapper (`HtmlDocument` from blitz-html, `DioxusDocument` from dioxus-native) (packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:); it holds the DOM tree, CSS parsing and resolution, layout and event handling, while html parsing (blitz-html), networking (blitz-net), rendering (blitz-paint) and windowing (blitz-shell) live in separate crates (packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:); its native Rust API is designed for higher-level abstractions, so any implementor can interact with the DOM and render it with any renderer (packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:)
  - blitz-traits holds types and traits enabling interoperability between the other Blitz crates "without circular or unnecessary dependencies" (packages/blitz-traits/src/lib.rs:)
  - blitz-paint pushes anyrender drawing commands into an impl PaintScene, and the PaintScene implementation decides whether to rasterize, emit SVG/PDF, or serialize the commands (packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs:); painting assumes styles and layout are already resolved (packages/blitz-paint/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:); an open select's list is painted by `paint_select_list` after the root's render inside `paint_scene`, from the public read `select_list_view`, reaching a shell or renderer through `paint_scene` alone, and its rows' text is the carve-out, laid out at paint through the public `select_row_layout`, only the rows in the scrollport (packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:; packages/blitz-paint/src/render/select_list.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:)

- **One incremental pipeline, safe identities** — style, damage, box construction, layout and paint topology are invalidated incrementally through a single code path, over versioned node ids.
  - Incremental and non-incremental layout run the same style → damage → box construction → layout pipeline; non-incremental marks every node damaged each resolve (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:), so the two must produce identical layouts after any sequence of mutations (tests/blitz-tests/tests/incremental_oracle.rs:)
  - Blitz runs a style pass then a separate layout pass (unlike Servo, which interleaves them), accepting it is slower because it is fast enough (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:); inline (Parley) layout construction is deferred to a dedicated phase so text shaping can be multithreaded (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:)
  - The paint tree holds topology only, built once per frame after layout for damaged subtrees; geometry is derived at use time from `final_layout()` and memoised per geometry generation so a cached list cannot paint a box where layout no longer puts it (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/paint_tree.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/paint_tree_incremental.rs:)
  - Style changes are classified into damage bits and only nodes whose subtree needs relayout have their layout caches cleared (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs:); state changes (hover/focus/active/disabled) set no restyle hint and invalidation is driven by element snapshots (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:)
  - Device changes (resize, zoom, color-scheme, media type) are coalesced so the stylist device is rebuilt at most once per resolve (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_device.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_device.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/device_coalescing.rs:); a viewport resize invalidates only origins whose media query results changed and elements using viewport units (tests/blitz-tests/tests/resize_restyle.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/resize_restyle.rs:)
  - Text decoration styles are kept out of Parley so they can change without rebuilding the Parley layout, read lazily at render time (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_parley.rs:); user-initiated and programmatic scrolls share one scrolling primitive, differing only in the `ScrollRequest` (packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:), an open select list's rows standing apart from it: a wheel over the list and `scroll_into_view` on a row move the list's own `scroll_y`, the latter writing it at once and returning with no chain or viewport moving (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:)
  - Node storage is a versioned slotmap so a dropped node's id stops resolving instead of aliasing a reused slot (packages/blitz-dom/src/tree.rs:); the slotmap key is used only at the storage boundary and all public APIs use `NodeId` (packages/blitz-dom/src/tree.rs:); persistent interaction state references DOM nodes only, never layout-generated nodes, so it survives box-tree reconstruction (tests/blitz-tests/tests/interaction_state_canonicalization.rs:)

 `Session::start(label: &str, boot: impl FnOnce() -> Harness<DioxusDocument>) -> Result<Session, SessionError>` validates the label first — 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, else `InvalidLabel` with the boot not run — then runs the caller's boot once on the calling thread and owns the harness it returns, offering `label()`, `harness()`, `harness_mut()` and `act(step: impl FnOnce(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>)) -> Result<Settled, SessionError>`, which runs the step on the held instance, settles it through the load wait (below: `Harness::settle`, the Test harness contract above, settled again while a load is in flight, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`) and maps an instance that did not go quiet onto `NotSettled(Busy)` — the step is not rolled back, and nothing `act` reads or returns crosses the socket; `with_time(self, step: impl FnMut(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>, u32) + 'static) -> Session` returns the session carrying a caller's time step — handed the held harness and the milliseconds an `advance` asks for, it moves the app's own time and returns nothing, the session itself moving the harness's clock on every `advance` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — and a session started without it carries none; the session holds a label, the harness, that optional step, one private record of the ids its screens have read and the optional crate-private recording `recording_into` sets (stated with `run`, below) — no `NodeId`, no viewport, font or scheme setting, no subscriber, and it neither reads nor drains the changed set; the crate names no app and no stand type, so the boot and the time step are the caller's (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:).
 `serve(state_dir: &Path, session: Session, idle_expiry: Duration) -> Result<(), SessionError>` hosts one session for the life of a process: it prepares the state directory and its socket as §Occupied Resources records (a socket file no process answers on is replaced, one a process answers on is `AlreadyRunning`, a path `std` refuses as too long is `StateDirTooLong`), answers one connection at a time on the calling thread with a 2 s read and write bound each — its accept loop non-blocking, polled every 25 ms — runs a `call` request through `Session::run` and nothing else, answering with the outcome or the refusal as one line of JSON, and on `stop`, or once no request has been answered for `idle_expiry`, drops the session and removes the socket file and the directory; every answered request — a refused or malformed one included — counts toward `served` and starts the idle count again, and a connection that breaks before its request is whole does neither; `IDLE_EXPIRY`, what a command line's host serves under, is 1,800 s (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:).
 The lifecycle another process drives, and the call it sends: `attach(state_dir) -> Result<Hello, SessionError>` with `Hello { pid: u32, label: String, served: u64, idle_expiry_s: u64 }` — no socket file reads `NoSession`, a socket nothing answers on `Dead`, an answer outside the protocol `Protocol`; `stop(state_dir)` sends the stop request and waits, at most 5 s, until the state directory is gone (`Timeout` past it); `start(state_dir, host: std::process::Command, ready: Duration) -> Result<Started, SessionError>` with `Started { child: std::process::Child, hello: Hello }` attaches first (answered reads `AlreadyRunning`, nothing spawned), spawns `host` as configured and polls every 25 ms until the session answers, the host exits (`HostExited(code)`) or `ready` passes (`Timeout`, the host killed and reaped); it does not check that the answering pid is the child it spawned; `call(state_dir, call: &Call) -> Result<Answer, SessionError>` with `Answer { accepted: bool, json: String }` sends one call and returns its answer — it runs `validate` first, so a call the schema refuses is answered there with its refusal and reaches no session, and every call sent fits the request bound; the answer is read under a 30 s bound on each read (`Timeout` past it; pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by the unix-only `client::imp::tests::an_answer_read_past_its_bound_is_a_timeout`, which reads the bound equal to `wire::ANSWER_BOUND`, 30 s, and a read past a shortened bound on a listener that never answers as `Timeout`), an `oversize` reply reads as `AnswerTooLarge` — the call ran, and what it did is not rolled back — and with no session to reach it reads as `attach` does (packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:).

 The wire is crate-private and versioned `v3`: one request line and one reply line per connection, `\n`-terminated — requests `hello v3`, `stop v3` and `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` (kinds `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value percent-escaped byte for byte — every byte but an ASCII letter, a digit, `-`, `_`, `.` and `~` — and decoded strictly: uppercase hex only, no escape of a byte that needs none, the decoded bytes UTF-8, a number in its one spelling), at most 16,384 bytes where `v1` admitted 64, the widest call the schema admits being 15,360 bytes of values; replies `ok v3 pid={pid} label={label} served={n} idle_expiry_s={s}`, `ok v3 stopping`, `refused version` (a known word with another version) and `refused malformed` (anything else, a call the decoder does not read included), at most 128 bytes — the widest `hello` measures 122 — and, to a call, `ok v3 accepted <json>`, `ok v3 refused <json>`, `ok v3 oversize` or `ok v3 recording-failed` — sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed` — an answer bounded at 1,048,576 bytes on its JSON line alone and `frame` the one function that turns an answer into its reply; `{n}` counts every request the host answered before this one, refusals included; a refusal or a broken connection changes nothing, an `oversize` reply is no refusal — the call ran and what it did stands — and a `stop` takes effect once its reply is written (packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:). ## 2026-10-05-fork-ci-reached — upstream-only signing, WPT and dispatch; the fork's cache budget
**Section:** §Occupied Resources (CI infrastructure · Outbound hosts) · §Standard Contracts (CI contracts) · §Infrastructure Patterns (Deployment model · CI/CD) · §Inherited Defaults (Deployment)
**Change:** was "Signed Builds" / "WPT" environments, the warp runner, the Pages deploy, the `update-results` dispatch and browser bundling reached by ref (main / `ci-test`) in this repository; now every job that reaches them — `release-cli`, `wpt`, `trigger-archive`, `post-results` — carries `github.repository == 'DioxusLabs/blitz'`, so no fork ref reaches the environments, their secrets, the Pages deploy, the dispatch or the WPT report fetch; the ref-keyed expressions inside stand, unreachable on the fork. CI infrastructure adds the fork's Actions cache: 12 entries, ≈ 9.73 GB of the 10 GB per-repository budget (LRU eviction) after the first build-branch run — one rust cache per compiling ci.yml job (11) plus one apt cache — as measured, so a lockfile or toolchain change mints new keys and evicts.
**Why:** a ref-only `if:` re-arms signing on the fork's own `main` and its existing `ci-test/sign-android-builds` branch, and the fork holds no secrets or environments; a repository guard keeps upstream's behaviour byte-equal and future upstream merges small (removing the workflows was rejected).
