title: security-plan
Threat Model Summary

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/threat-model-summary.md — read whole.
**Security tier:** `0`

> NOT YET MEASURED — no slice states an application-level threat model; data classification, auth model, infrastructure and compliance triggers were not gathered for this summary (the stored-data and auth facts the reading did reach are in the sections below).
**Attack surface:**

- **Vector:** remote web content (HTML, CSS, images, fonts, sub-documents) — the browser and its net provider fetch and parse arbitrary remote documents, `file:` and `data:` URLs, SVG data and sub-documents; iframe and `@import` nesting depths are limited and stale iframe responses discarded by request id; per-input checks are listed under Input Validation.

- **Vector:** script execution — `blitz-vibey-script` executes a document's scripts, `<body onload>` included, and JS `fetch()` and module imports share its ScriptFetcher; in the browser app JavaScript is opt-in behind the non-default `javascript` feature, and the WPT runner executes test scripts; the default fetcher takes only `file:` and `data:` URLs, every runtime event reads `isTrusted` true, and same-origin or CORS checks are observed absent.

- **Vector:** CLI input
  - **Entry point:** `screenshot` and `paint_bench` fetch and render an arbitrary URL given on the command line (examples/screenshot.rs:; examples/paint_bench.rs:). `preact_script` executes the scripts of an arbitrary local HTML file given on the command line (examples/preact_script.rs:). rdme fetches remote URLs and treats a `.md` suffix as markdown (apps/readme/src/main.rs:)
  - **Trust boundary:** argument parsing is listed under Input Validation.

- **Vector:** markdown rendering (rdme)
  - **Entry point:** rdme's comrak renderer sets `unsafe: true`, passing raw HTML in markdown through (apps/readme/src/markdown/comrak.rs:)

- **Vector:** WPT runner local file reads
  - **Entry point:** Non-`data:` request URLs have their path joined onto the WPT base path and the file is read (wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:)

- **Vector:** CI workflow triggered by pull requests
  - **Entry point / Trust boundary:** The post-results workflow runs only in `DioxusLabs/blitz` (repository guard), only for successful `pull_request`-triggered WPT runs, and checks out scripts from the default branch, a step named "Checkout trusted scripts" (.github/workflows/wpt-post-results.yml:; .github/workflows/wpt-post-results.yml:)

- **Vector:** local IPC — the driver session's socket — `escher_driver::serve` binds one Unix-domain socket, `session.sock`, in a caller-named state directory, no TCP or UDP port, unix only; trust boundary the owning user (directory `0700`, a group- or other-open one refused, socket `0600`), no other authentication; it carries the lifecycle and calls with their answers — ids, names, control values (a password's or file input's masked), snapshot text, diffs, screenshots, a lint's findings — and no `NodeId`.

- **Vector:** local stdio — the driver's MCP server — `escher-session mcp`, a stdio child an MCP client spawns, speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 on its stdin and stdout, no listener, port or socket; trust boundary the spawning client process, no authentication; a result carries ids, names, control values (a password's or file input's masked), snapshot text, diffs, screenshots and a lint's findings to the client, and what a client does with them, a model provider included, is the client's — the cold-agent live runs carried the screen so, a screenshot and a lint's findings among it.

title: Authentication & Authorization

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/authentication-authorization.md — read whole.
**Auth approach:** none observed. Application authentication or authorization code is observed absent in every slice that searched:
The s02 fixtures hold no auth code; the google fixture only shows a "Sign in" link to accounts.google.com (examples/assets/google.html:).

Auth controls by requirement: with feature `cookies` the reqwest client keeps a cookie store; CI tokens are scoped by GitHub Actions `permissions` per workflow — every ci.yml job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` read-only, the publish job repository-guarded so no fork ref reaches its "Signed Builds" environment or its secrets.

The driver session socket and the MCP stdio server carry no handshake, token, secret or peer check: the socket's access is the filesystem's (state directory `0700`, a group- or other-open one refused, socket `0600`), and `start` does not check the answering pid; the MCP server answers only the process holding its stdin and stdout and binds nothing.
Other `password` occurrences are not credentials:

- A `password` accessor (the URL password component) is defined on the element prototype for `<a>`/`<area>`, read from and written into the resolved `href` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/hyperlink.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/hyperlink.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/hyperlink.rs:)
- An `<input type="password">` fixture is mapped to `Role::PasswordInput` in an accessibility test (tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_roles.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_roles.rs:)

title: Input Validation

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/input-validation.md — read whole.

CLI arguments (examples) — numeric arguments fall back to defaults; a URL (retried with `https://`) or `preact_script` path that cannot be resolved panics, as does an unknown `multi_doc` mode; an output filename keeps only the URL's ASCII alphanumerics.

CLI arguments (agent-run.sh) — a verb outside `boot run status cleanup logs`, a wrong argument count or a selection other than `stand`, `all` or an existing test-file stem prints usage and exits 2 before any cargo call.

CLI arguments (cold-agent.sh) — a verb outside `run status cleanup logs`, a wrong argument count or a task outside the allowlist `stand` exits 2 before any precondition or `claude` call; the task reaches the agent session only as the fixed prompt, naming no element id and no app slug.

CLI arguments (apt-install.sh) — package names and option values must match closed forms, else usage and exit 2 before `sudo`, `timeout`, `apt-get` or `dpkg` runs; the script reads no environment variable of its own, writes no file and names no secret; every attempt after the first runs a bounded `dpkg --configure -a` repair.

CLI arguments (coverage_floor.py) — each floor must match `CRATE_DIR=PERCENT` (a percent at most 100, no crate twice) and every crate must have an `SF` record, else exit 2; it prints only crate directories and counts, never a source or lcov path.

Cold-agent check (cold-agent.sh, the agent-written check) — the model's reply is a new input class: only its last fenced json block, bounded in bytes and steps, each step checked against closed keys; a check outside these is never replayed, a valid one replayed on fresh `escher-session mcp` children, every step validated again by the server under a reply bound; `check.json` is never printed; the live child's kept checks (`--record`) are read for bools and counts only and never printed, and a paged answer is decoded only as exactly `text` · `part` · `parts`.

Driver session socket (escher-driver) — one request line per connection, parsed against a closed grammar under a size bound; anything else is refused with nothing run, and a decoded call runs through `Session::run` alone; one connection at a time under fixed bounds; bounded replies carry ids, names, control values (a password's or file input's masked), snapshot text, diffs, screenshots and a lint's findings, the state readings as closed words and booleans, never an attribute's text, and no `NodeId`.

Driver session socket (escher-driver) — the widening rule: a new field of a closed value set inside an already ratified carrier is not a boundary widening, while a field holding authored text, an open value set, a new carrier or a new exit still is.

Driver session state directory (escher-driver) — created `0700`, a present one open to its group or others refused, the socket `0600`, a path too long for a socket address refused with a fixed message holding no path; only the socket file and then the directory are ever deleted, non-recursively; the path is a parameter, never an env read or a cwd-relative default.

Driver recording directory (escher-driver) — created `0700`, a group- or other-open one refused with nothing written or spawned; each check created `0600` and never replaced; a failed write or a passed bound ends the recording; a file the recorder did not create is never removed; unix only; no tool call, verb, argument or result field names the directory, and nothing of it is logged.

Recorded check (escher-driver `Check::from_bytes`) — a kept check's bytes are untrusted: a strict reader bounded in bytes and records, with closed keys and schema-named arguments, anything else refused `malformed` holding nothing of the file, with no panic path; every replayed step still passes `validate` inside `Session::run`.
Driver session label (escher-driver) — 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, checked before the caller's boot runs; never text read from the document; the one caller string a reply carries.

Driver command schema (escher-driver) — `validate` checks every call against a closed `'static` table of twelve verbs and seven bounded argument kinds, returning a typed `Command` or a `Refusal`, the first failure in a fixed order; nothing public runs a `Command` that did not come from `validate`, and the socket, the command line and MCP all pass through it; an `id` naming no element, or an element that cannot take the call, is refused with nothing run.

Driver command schema (escher-driver) — no `unwrap`, `expect` or panic on anything a call supplies, no clock read by the schema or its validation, no `NodeId` kept between calls; one `command` span per call holds fixed words, bools and counts only, never a call's content, the screen text, an image or findings; the crate installs no subscriber and reads no env var.

CLI arguments (escher-session) — the argv is read by `escher_driver::command_line`, a closed reader with fixed rules; a call is checked by `validate` or `validate_session` before the session address is asked for; four endings with fixed statuses (0 accepted, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 session error); no ending writes back anything the caller typed, no path on argv panics, and the command line installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable.

MCP server (escher-driver `serve_mcp`, the `escher-session mcp` role) — newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on the invoking user's stdin and stdout, no listener, port, authentication or env read; request lines and results bounded; protocol errors a fixed code and message with no `data`; tool arguments typed, then `validate` or `validate_session`; the admitted request `id` the one client-sent value written back; no print, `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside the tests.
Browser urlbar — typed text is parsed as a URL, then as a dotted space-free host with https, else turned into a search query.
Navigation to external browser — limited to GET requests with http, https or mailto schemes.
Link `href` — resolved against the document URL; an unparseable href is not navigated.
Document URL — a parse error is returned instead of a panic.
URL fragment — percent-decoded lossily before matching.
`file:` URLs (net provider) — read from local disk with no path restriction; a `file:` URL that is no file path is a typed error, no panic.
`data:` URLs (net provider) — decoded by the `data_url` crate, errors mapped to `ProviderError`.
`data:` URLs (shell) — only the `data` scheme is handled; a failed parse or decode returns silently.

Script fetch — invalid `data:` URLs or non-UTF-8 script bytes are `FetchError::InvalidData`; a `file:` URL loads only for a `file:` document, `fetch()`, a module `import` and `<script src>` each refused otherwise with a `FetchError` — a narrowing: the default fetcher takes only `file:` and `data:`, and same-origin and CORS checks are absent.
Script type — only an empty, `text/javascript`, `application/javascript` or `module` type is executed.
HTML parsing — HTML is parsed with scripting disabled.
Fetched stylesheets — must be valid UTF-8, else the load errs; a failed, empty or non-CSS stylesheet blocks no render.
Stylesheet `href` — an `href` that cannot be resolved starts no load, no panic, and blocks no render.
Fetched iframe HTML — decoded lossily as UTF-8.
Fetched images — decoded with a guessed format, then an SVG parse fallback, else an error.
Favicon — accepted only when it decodes as a raster image or SVG.
Fetched fonts — the format is sniffed from the first four bytes when no hint is given; bytes shorter than 4 pass through, and a failed WOFF decompression keeps the original bytes.

`@font-face` source — a source whose URL cannot be resolved is skipped, no panic; a hint-less source with no extension (a `data:` URL) is fetched and its format sniffed; escher routes no agent- or user-supplied URL through this path.
SVG data — non-UTF-8 input rejected, XML parsed with DTDs allowed, gzip-compressed SVG detected and decompressed before parsing.
SVG `viewBox` — exactly four finite non-negative numbers; a zero width or height is flagged degenerate.
Inline SVG source — a parse error is logged and the element left without image data.
CSS declarations — validated by parsing: invalid declarations are ignored, and unsupported property names or invalid values refused.
Selectors — an invalid selector list leaves the rule unchanged; query parse errors are returned.
`<style>` element — HTML entities are decoded before parsing.
Legacy attributes — `bgcolor`, dimensions, SVG `width` / `height`, `border` and body margin pass closed parsers; anything else is ignored or rejected.

Markup numeric attributes — parsed with default fallbacks; `rowspan` clamped to 1..=65534, `size` on a `multiple` select capped at 65534 with `0` or a non-numeric value no hint, `<ol start>` parsed as `usize`; the `size` read is an engine change for every document and a boundary widening, ratified.

Markup attributes — read from parsed content, remote pages included, by in-process readers with no log site or panic path: `disabled` and `inert` by presence, ARIA states and closed values through closed parses carrying no attribute text, the range and select controls held within their rules, Enter activating buttons and links and Space buttons as a click, Enter and Space opening a single select's engine-painted list, Space only with no typed text standing, names and descriptions as page text, an option's and a group's label also painted in an open list; they leave escher only by the ratified carriers, the page's own form submission and events aside; the list's keys and painted labels are an engine change for every document and a boundary widening, ratified.

Markup attributes — the stable element id: the HTML `id` as an author key when non-empty, `/`-free and first in document order, else an anchored, component or document path, so no `id` can make two ids equal; computed on demand and written by escher's code to no log, it leaves by the platform adapter, the driver's answers, MCP results and kept checks, and no `NodeId` crosses.

Markup attributes — a password's or file input's value reads as the fixed `MASKED_VALUE` in the snapshot, its text, diffs and every carrier, never the text, its length or a file's host path; a password input paints a bullet per character, and a recorded masked `type` is kept as `MASKED_STAND_IN`; the DOM and form submission keep the value.
Layout values — degenerate aspect ratios are discarded, inline-box heights kept finite, and `text_extent` is a read-only reader returning geometry only.
Paint values — non-finite geometry is culled, gradient overflow clamped, oversized radii scaled down, and hidden inputs not painted.
Scrolling — targets are clamped to the scroll range; a programmatic scroll to a missing node does nothing.
Forms — `method` and `enctype` fall back to defaults; submitted controls are filtered, line endings normalized to CRLF, and a file input's `accept` is not applied as a filter.
Forms (dioxus-native) — form data validity is not implemented: `NativeFormData::valid` always returns true.
Dioxus mutations — `data-dioxus-id` parsed as `usize`, unsupported attribute value types ignored, falsy boolean attributes removed, and `dangerous_inner_html` applied with `set_inner_html`.

JS API arguments — the script runtime's native APIs check or coerce their arguments, throwing a RangeError, TypeError, SyntaxError or JS error on a bad call or falling back to a default; `fetch()` takes GET or HEAD only.
Persistence (sqlite) — values are bound through `params!` placeholders; stored URLs re-parsed on load, unparsable rows skipped.
Serialization output — text and attribute values are escaped, but raw-text elements' text is written unescaped; inline SVG must serialize as well-formed XML.
Test harness queries — selector parsing returns a `Result`, while the harness query helper panics on an invalid selector; a text or comment scope matches nothing.

WPT runner — quarantine entries, fuzzy ranges, `checkLayout` values, `data:` URLs and page messages are checked, a bad entry panicking, dropped or failing its test or request; wrapper HTML is escaped; only JavaScript script types run.
CI scripts — the PR lookup takes only an open PR whose head sha equals the run's, and the comment splice replaces only when both markers exist in order.
Example apps — the 7GUIs inputs, the widget's `color` attribute and the TodoMVC input are validated or fall back.
Example fixtures — the graphite and google fixtures constrain their form inputs (required, `type=email`, `maxlength`).

title: Data Protection

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/data-protection.md — read whole.
**In transit:**
- **TLS:** TLS is provided through reqwest's `native-tls` feature (`native-tls-vendored` on Android) (packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml:)
- Encryption or TLS code is observed absent in s10 — searched: `encrypt|cipher|rustls|tls` over the 32 s10 files — and in s11 — searched: `encrypt|crypt|tls|rustls|cert` over the 21 listed s11 files.
> NOT YET MEASURED — HSTS, TLS version requirements and certificate pinning: no slice gathered them.
**At rest — per medium:**

- **Database:** History is written to a sqlite file opened with `Connection::open` (apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:). Database encryption is observed absent — searched: `encrypt|cipher|sqlcipher` (case-insensitive) over the 86 s04 files. On mobile, history is in-memory only and does not persist across launches (apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:)

- **Files / object storage (HTTP cache):** With feature `cache`, HTTP responses are cached on disk through `CACacheManager` at the platform cache directory (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:); the cache policy is evaluated as a private (`shared: false`) cache (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:). Cookies and HTTP cache are default browser features (apps/browser/Cargo.toml:; apps/browser/Cargo.toml:)

- **Files (kept checks):** under `--record <dir>` on `escher-session` or `Session::recording_into`, one `check-{n}.json` (`0600`) per recorded session in a `0700` directory the launcher named — per call its verb, arguments, acceptance, digest and masked answer, never a pixel; owner-only, except the two committed checks (below); never logged, never removed by escher but for its own check when a recording ends; the cold-agent pipe's live child keeps its checks so in the owner-only `target/cold-agent/record/`, read by the pipe for bools and counts only, never printed, copied or committed, removed by its `cleanup`.

- **Files (committed checks):** two kept checks of the repository's own scripted stand-Counter sessions are committed, `tests/blitz-tests/checks/counter-cli.json` and `counter-mcp.json` — the one exception to a kept check's owner-only medium, holding no typed text, host path, name or secret and no `screenshot` step, read only through the strict `Check::from_bytes`; a check of any other session stays owner-only and is never committed.
- **Logs:** request URLs and the cache directory path are logged (see Logging & Monitoring)

- Encryption, redaction or sanitization of data is observed absent in s05 — searched: `encrypt|crypt|sanitiz|redact|scrub` over the 15 s05 files; escher's own log sink now redacts and, for a record from a target outside its allowlist, drops (escher-telemetry's target allowlist — see Logging & Monitoring).
**Local user data handled:**

- Copy writes the selected document text to the clipboard only when no text input is focused (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:); clipboard text is read and written through arboard on desktop OSes behind the clipboard feature (packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:)
- The native file dialog uses rfd with optional name/extension filters behind the file-dialog feature (packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:)

- A chosen file's full path is stored in the file input's `value` attribute (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:); `FormData` file entries carry a filesystem path that is serialized as its string form (packages/blitz-traits/src/net.rs:); the attribute and form submission keep the path, while under dioxus-native-dom's `accessibility` feature `DioxusDocument::snapshot` reads that value as `MASKED_VALUE`, so neither the snapshot, its text (`Snapshot::to_text`) nor a diff of two snapshots (`Snapshot::diff`, which takes its values from the snapshots only) holds it (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot.rs:; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/snapshot_diff.rs:) — the reader's half as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization/report.md on an authored `value`; the diff's half is by construction, no file-input diff having been run; the dialog's write of the path is read from the code, not run

- Fixtures: the google fixture sets a referrer meta of "origin" (examples/assets/google.html:); the servo fixtures show Cloudflare email-protection links (`/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection`) in place of plain addresses (examples/assets/servo-new.html:; examples/assets/servo.html:; examples/assets/servo.html:)
**Data lifecycle:**

- **Deletion:** The about:history page offers "Clear history", which deletes all rows in memory and on disk (apps/browser/src/about_pages.rs:; apps/browser/src/browser_history.rs:; apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:). A "Clear Cache" menu item calls `clear_cache` (apps/browser/src/toolbar.rs:); the cache can be cleared through `Provider::clear_cache` (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:)
> NOT YET MEASURED — key management, backups, retention periods and anonymization: no slice gathered them.

title: API Security

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/api-security.md — read whole.

No served network API exists — no served TCP or UDP port, two `blitz-net` tests alone binding TCP on loopback, served by no binary; the one listener is local, the driver session's Unix-domain socket `{state_dir}/session.sock`, and the `escher-session mcp` role serves the driver's verbs as MCP tools over its own stdin and stdout, binding nothing, under bounded requests and results; the controls below govern outbound requests and in-document navigation.

Outbound requests: at most 6 concurrent per host; caller-supplied headers forwarded with `User-Agent`; non-success statuses typed `ProviderError::HttpStatus`; cancellable through an `AbortSignal`; CORS and same-origin checks, CSP, a response size limit and a request timeout are observed absent.

Settle and loads in flight: a harness settle never waits on a load in flight, and the driver's acting step waits on one for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, so the absent request timeout cannot hang a settle or a command; no verb has an argument or a result field of a wait.

Navigation and fetch: sub-resource requests are GETs and JS-facing fetch GET or HEAD only; form submission goes by scheme and method, the `dialog` method rejected; iframe navigations route back to the parent document; external targets go to the system browser; the `dioxus` scheme is served from the local file system; dioxus-native JS evaluation goes to a no-op document.
Outbound HTTP in the examples and apps goes through reqwest or blitz-net; CI API calls go through the `gh api` CLI with the workflow token.

Local session socket: reachable by the owning user only (`0700` directory, `0600` socket, a group- or other-open directory refused), no handshake secret, token or peer-credential check; one connection at a time under fixed read, write and size bounds; a host that answers no request for its idle expiry ends as on `stop`.

Fixture pages also issue requests: the graphite fixture's script calls api.github.com with fetch and no request headers (examples/assets/graphite.html:); the servo.org snapshot fixture issues an XMLHttpRequest GET to `https://api.github.com/repos/servo/servo-nightly-builds/releases/latest` (examples/assets/servo.html:).

title: Dependency Security

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/dependency-security.md — read whole.

**Audit tool:** cargo-deny 0.20.2 — `cargo deny --locked --workspace --all-features check advisories licenses` over the whole workspace's graph, configured by the root `deny.toml` (the six platforms ci.yml builds, all features; ignores per ID only, each with a written reason, no blanket allow; `unsound` at its default, which keeps memmap2's unsound advisory out of the gate); each ignore re-read on every push; the reach is cargo-deny's resolved graph, not the whole lockfile.
**Pinning:**

- No git dependency is left in the root manifest: taffy, the one there was, pinned by commit rev until 2026-10-13-upstream-sync-polish-and-ship, is a crates.io registry version since that chunk, "0.15" resolved 0.15.0 with a checksum in `Cargo.lock` (Cargo.toml:); parley is a registry version, "0.12" (Cargo.toml:)

- Each upstream sync took upstream's dependency set whole or, by cherry-pick, entered no package — one of them moving lock edges alone (one `mimalloc` edge added, twelve re-pointed to versions already locked) beside a lock-only `tokio` update past RUSTSEC-2026-0386; its lock read name by name, against upstream's or against the tree before it, the audit leg green after it — one of them only with the zbus-family ignores (Audit tool).

- Builds pass `--locked` in the flake, in `dx bundle` and in every ci.yml cargo leg but `examples/wasm_hello`, which has no `Cargo.lock` (flake.nix:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh:; .github/workflows/ci.yml:)

- Most dependency versions are inherited with `workspace = true` (apps/browser/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-dom/Cargo.toml:); every dependency in the blitz-html and blitz-net manifests does so (packages/blitz-html/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml:), as do the blitz-traits and blitz manifests (packages/blitz-traits/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz/Cargo.toml:) and every dev-dependency of blitz-tests (tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml:)

- Inline versions outside the workspace: examples pin `idna_adapter` to exactly 1.0.0 (examples/counter/Cargo.toml:); android-activity is pinned at "0.6.0" in blitz-shell (packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml:); `cfg-if` is pinned at "1.0.4" and `android-activity` at "0.6" in dioxus-native (packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:; packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:); `log = "0.4"` is the one inline version in blitz-vibey-script (packages/blitz-vibey-script/Cargo.toml:); the WPT runner's non-workspace dependencies declare explicit versions, and `dify` and `wptreport` disable default features (wpt/runner/Cargo.toml:)
- rusqlite is built with its `bundled` feature (apps/browser/persistence/Cargo.toml:)

- `serde_json = "1"` is a root `[workspace.dependencies]` entry inherited by escher-driver with no feature (no `preserve_order`): the reader of the MCP server's untrusted stdin, of a kept check's bytes and of the driver's own answer line the replay compares, writing nothing; no ban list exists (§Security Anti-Patterns).

- `png` is taken by escher-driver, the encoder of a shot, and by blitz-tests as a dev-dependency; blitz-test-harness takes `blitz-paint`, `anyrender` and `anyrender_vello_cpu`; no package enters `Cargo.lock` and no `base64` crate is taken — a shot's base64 is written by hand.

- blitz-test-harness takes `color = { workspace = true }`, already in the graph through blitz-dom, as the luminance source of its contrast reader; no package enters `Cargo.lock`, and blitz-test-harness takes no `tracing` and no `style`.

- CI tooling: `cross` is installed from a pinned git rev; the upstream-only publish workflow installs dioxus-cli `0.8.0-alpha.3`, or on a platform flagged `use_git_cli` from git at upstream's pinned rev, behind its `DioxusLabs/blitz` repository guard; wpt cli is pinned to 0.0.14 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/wpt.yml:); ci.yml installs `cargo-deny@0.20.2` (the audit tool) and `cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1` (the coverage tool) through `taiki-e/install-action` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:; .github/workflows/ci.yml:); every ci.yml `uses:` is pinned to a 40-hex commit SHA with its ref kept as a trailing comment, asserted by `test_ci_workflows.py` (.github/scripts/test_ci_workflows.py:) — `awalsh128/cache-apt-pkgs-action` included (.github/workflows/ci.yml:); the upstream-only publish-browser and wpt workflows no longer use it: each installs its packages with a bare `apt-get` line, behind its `DioxusLabs/blitz` repository guard (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/wpt.yml:)

- Vendored JS: Preact is vendored as an unmodified copy of its UMD builds (examples/preact/index.html:); each vendored Preact file ends with a `sourceMappingURL` comment for a `.map` file (examples/preact/vendor/preact.min.js:; examples/preact/vendor/hooks.umd.js:)
- The blitz-tests crate is not published (`publish = false`) (tests/blitz-tests/Cargo.toml:)
**Update policy:** automated update tooling is observed absent — searched: `dependabot` over .github/workflows/*.yml, Cargo.toml, Cross.toml, flake.nix, .github/scripts/*.py.

**CI integration:** ci.yml's `audit` job ("Dependency audit") runs `bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh audit` on every pull request and push, in the slow tier behind the four fast jobs, uncached, its log uploaded on failure as `ci-log-audit` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:).

**Unsafe code:** `stylo_taffy` holds two `unsafe` blocks — one builds a taffy `LengthPercentage` from a raw calc pointer, and one, in its public `resolve_calc_value`, reads a calc value back through such a pointer (packages/stylo_taffy/src/convert.rs:; packages/stylo_taffy/src/convert.rs:); two `unsafe` raw-pointer operations exist for calc values in layout (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/table.rs:)
> NOT YET MEASURED — a critical-CVE response SLA: none is stated. The lockfile's advisory state is read on every push by the audit leg, within cargo-deny's resolved graph (Audit tool above).

title: Supply chain integrity

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/dependency-security.md — read whole.

- **Signed artifacts:** The publish job runs only in `DioxusLabs/blitz` and there uses environment "Signed Builds" only on main or `ci-test` branches, so the fork produces no signed artifact (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:); a macOS signing key and an Android keystore are written from secrets for the build and removed in `always()` steps (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:)

- **Lockfile verification:** builds pass `--locked` (flake.nix:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:), and so does every ci.yml cargo leg — the leg script's build, test, clippy (both lines), doc, msrv, counter, wasm, audit, a11y, coverage and, since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, stand-repeat commands and the matrix command — except `examples/wasm_hello`, a standalone workspace with no `Cargo.lock` (.github/scripts/ci-leg.sh:; .github/workflows/ci.yml:)

- **Subresource integrity (fixtures):** the gosub fixture's Font Awesome link carries an integrity hash with crossorigin=anonymous and referrerpolicy=no-referrer (examples/assets/gosub.html:); the servo.org snapshot fixture loads jQuery with an `integrity` hash and `crossorigin="anonymous"` (examples/assets/servo.html:); other remote stylesheets are linked without integrity attributes (examples/assets/pseudo.html:; examples/assets/newservo.html:; examples/assets/servo-new-reduced.html:; examples/assets/servo-new.html:; examples/assets/servo-new.html:) — integrity attributes outside gosub.html are observed absent, searched: `integrity=` over the 21 s02 files; the servo.org snapshot fixture references third-party CDN resources: Font Awesome v5.12.0, Google Fonts, prismjs@1.20.0 on unpkg, jquery-3.4.1 on code.jquery.com (examples/assets/servo.html:; examples/assets/servo.html:)

- **Licence compliance:** the root `deny.toml` holds upstream's `[licenses]` table byte for byte, and the audit leg runs it on every push over the whole workspace's graph, so the fork gates on licences; upstream's own `licenses` job stays reverted.
> NOT YET MEASURED — SBOM generation and base image scanning: no slice gathered them.

title: Bootstrap phases (derive for route / setup-project)

body: - **auth-scaffolding-baseline:** authentication or authorization code is recorded absent — see Authentication & Authorization.
- **dep-audit-tooling-install:** discharged — cargo-deny 0.20.2 with the root `deny.toml` is the audit tool — see Dependency Security.

- **logging-redaction-wire:** discharged for escher's own log sink — `escher_telemetry::init`'s target allowlist redacts engine-target messages and fields, redacts the content-named fields of escher targets, and drops every record from a target outside its two prefix sets at every level, in the two binaries that install it, `seven_guis_native` and `escher-session` (the drop delivered by the route entry "Sink target allowlist", the founder's ruling, 2026-10-07) — see Logging & Monitoring; still open for the upstream apps' `fmt::init()` stdout subscribers and the WPT runner's `env_logger`, which stay unscrubbed.
- **dep-security-ci-gate:** discharged — ci.yml's `audit` job runs the audit on every push — see Dependency Security.

title: Secret Management

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/secret-management.md — read whole.
**Storage:**

- **Production (CI):** secrets live in GitHub Actions secrets and vars — a macOS signing key and an Android keystore written from secrets for the build and removed in `always()` steps, the Apple certificate and keystore passwords passed from secrets, and the `WPT_GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` tokens passed to the steps that use them.

- **Development (operator host, the cold-agent live run and the MCP live trial only):** both reach the model provider through the operator's own Claude Code login, held by the `claude` CLI outside the repository — no API key, no env read by the pipe, no CI secret, no new secret source and no auth library; the committed live evidence holds no key, auth header, credential-file name, token field or e-mail address.
**Never in code:** secret reads in source are observed absent in every slice that searched:
**Environment values read (none secret-bearing):**

- `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` at build time (examples/screenshot.rs:), in a test (packages/blitz-vibey-script/tests/preact.rs:), since 2026-10-19-session-recording in escher-driver's unit tests, which reach the workspace `target/tmp` through it (packages/escher-driver/src/mcp_tests.rs:) and in upstream's `tests/all.rs` of blitz-tests, a target held at `test = false` and never built (tests/blitz-tests/tests/all.rs:)
- `HOME`, used for the iOS cache path (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:)
- `PAINT_TREE_BENCH_HTML`, an HTML file path for an ignored benchmark (tests/blitz-tests/tests/paint_tree_bench.rs:)

- `MULTI_DOC_N`, `MULTI_DOC_SEQ` and `MULTI_DOC_FLAT`, read by the root example `multi_doc` alone through two `std::env::var` call sites: a document count parsed with a default fallback and two flags read through its `env_flag` (examples/multi_doc.rs:; examples/multi_doc.rs:; examples/multi_doc.rs:; examples/multi_doc.rs:)
- `WPT_DIR` (plus compile-time `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`) (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:; wpt/runner/src/main.rs:)
- `RUST_LOG`, the tracing filter directives escher-telemetry's `EnvFilter` reads, defaulting to `warn` when unset or unparsable — not secret (packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:)

- `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_escher-session")` and `env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")` at build time in the session checks — the host binary's path and the directory their state directories live under; the escher-driver library's code and the `escher-session` binary read no env var beyond `RUST_LOG` through `escher_telemetry::init` (examples/seven_guis/tests/host_binary.rs:; examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:; examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/session_common/mod.rs:)

- `TMPDIR`, through `std::env::temp_dir()` — on unix that variable, else `/tmp` — at two test-only sites: escher-driver's unix-only client unit test `client::imp::tests`, which places its test-only listener's directory `eab-{pid}` there and removes it at the end — a `UnixListener` that accepts one connection and never answers, served by no binary and reached by no caller, so no crossing — and blitz-vibey-script's `tests/dom.rs` helper `temp_dir_with_files`, which makes the directory of files its `file:`-load tests read; test code only, not secret (packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/tests/dom.rs:; since 2026-10-14-quality-gates, registered as test-only on the operator's answer at that chunk's wrap, 2026-10-15)
**Fixture tokens:** the google fixture carries an http-equiv origin-trial meta with an encoded value (examples/assets/google.html:)

**What counts as secret (as observed):** CI signing material — the macOS signing key, the Android keystore and its passwords, the Apple certificate and its password — and the `WPT_GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` tokens (see Storage above); on the operator host, the operator's Claude Code login the cold-agent live run and the 2026-10-10-mcp-surface live trial use, held by the `claude` CLI — no artifact, event or verdict carries it.

title: Error Handling

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/error-handling.md — read whole.
**External responses (to end users):**
- A failed fetch renders `error.html` with the error's Debug text in the `#error` paragraph (apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs:; apps/browser/assets/error.html:)

- An empty response body renders the bundled 404 page and is flagged `is_error` (apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs:; apps/browser/assets/404.html:); error pages skip history recording and favicon probing (apps/browser/src/tab.rs:)

- CLI tools exit with status 1 after an stderr message: rdme when the argument is neither URL nor file, or no README.md is found (apps/readme/src/main.rs:; apps/readme/src/main.rs:); `paint_bench` prints `Unknown backend ...` for an unknown backend (examples/paint_bench.rs:)

- Fixtures: the graphite fixture's stars script wraps the fetch in try/catch and removes the target element on any failure (examples/assets/graphite.html:); the iframe page A fixture links to a missing page labelled "Broken link (should stay usable)" (examples/assets/iframe_page_a.html:)
**Internal logging (errors logged and dropped):**

- Persistence errors are logged at warn and swallowed; callers never see a `Result` (apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:; apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:; apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:)

- Failed resource loads are logged (under `tracing`) and dropped; pending image waiters for the URL are removed (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); a failed stylesheet's request leaves `pending_critical_resources`, so it blocks no render (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:)
- An unresolvable iframe `src` is logged and skipped (packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:); WOFF decompression failure is logged and the original bytes are kept (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:)

- In `NetProvider::fetch`, a failed fetch is logged when tracing is enabled and handed to the handler through `NetHandler::error`, a default that does nothing, with or without tracing (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-traits/src/net.rs:); a failure to clear the cache is logged at error level when tracing is enabled, and otherwise discarded (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:)
- Parse errors are collected into `DocumentHtmlParser::errors` and emitted at error level only with feature `tracing` (packages/blitz-html/src/html_sink.rs:; packages/blitz-html/src/html_sink.rs:)

- `eval`/`eval_module` log but do not propagate uncaught errors (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/modules.rs:); script URL resolve or fetch failures are recorded and that script is skipped (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:)

- A failed asset fetch is logged at warn and the handler is not called (packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:); a failure to open a URL is logged at error (packages/dioxus-native/src/link_handler.rs:)

- Unsupported winit variants fall back to a default value and log tracing::error when tracing is enabled (packages/blitz-shell/src/convert_events.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/convert_events.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:)
- Table descendants without styles are skipped with an info log rather than a panic (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/table.rs:)

- Results discarded outright: channel send results with `let _ =` (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/iframe.rs:); the clipboard write result (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:); IME update and window drag results (packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:); the proxy's channel send result (packages/blitz-shell/src/event.rs:)
**Error format (typed errors):**

- Stylo `RulesMutateError` values map to `CssomError` (packages/blitz-dom/src/cssom.rs:); CSSOM errors map to DOMException names, and `selectorText` and `cssText` assignment never throws (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/stylesheet.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/stylesheet.rs:)

- `FetchError` implements `Display` with scheme, IO, invalid-data and forbidden-load messages, and `std::error::Error` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/fetch.rs:); module resolve or fetch failures become JS TypeErrors (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/modules.rs:)

- `ClipboardError` is a unit struct with a TODO to "fill out with meaningful errors" (packages/blitz-traits/src/shell.rs:); arboard::Clipboard::new is unwrapped while get/set errors are mapped to ClipboardError (packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/lib.rs:)

- Missing nodes in mounted-element operations return `MountedError::OperationFailed` wrapping `NodeNotExistErr` (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:)
- WPT runner net errors are typed as `WptNetProviderError` (Io, DataUrl, DataUrlBase64, HandlerPanic) and logged with `warn!` (wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:; wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:)
- wasm_hello maps event-loop errors into `JsValue` (examples/wasm_hello/src/lib.rs:; examples/wasm_hello/src/lib.rs:)

- `gh_api` runs `subprocess.run(..., check=True)`, raising on non-zero exit (.github/scripts/wpt_diff_to_pr.py:); CI matrix jobs set `fail-fast: false` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:)

- escher-driver's command refusal is a typed value, `Refusal`: a closed set of eight causes, each with a fixed name, meaning and remedy holding no path, and a `Fault` only beside `malformed`; no `String` field, so a refusal cannot hold anything a call supplied; a `SessionError` is written from a fixed table likewise; MCP protocol errors are fixed codes and messages with no `data`; of a refusal only its cause's fixed name reaches a log.
**Graceful degradation (no panic):**

- Stale node ids in layout children are skipped rather than panicking (packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:); stale node ids resolve to `None` through `get` (packages/blitz-dom/src/tree.rs:)

- `resolve` and hit testing return early with a warning when there is no DOM (packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); `handle_ui_event` returns early when a document has no event target (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/driver.rs:)

- `stylo_to_cursor_icon` returns a default cursor for `Auto` instead of panicking (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_cursor_icon.rs:); an unknown alignment flag is mapped rather than panicking — to Taffy's `AlignContent::NORMAL` for content alignment, to none for item alignment (packages/stylo_taffy/src/convert.rs:; packages/stylo_taffy/src/convert.rs:)
- An unrecognized font format yields `Resource::None`, with a comment asking whether it should be an error (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:)

- `try_doc` returns `None` when the document is mutably borrowed (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:); `try_element_to_node_id` returns an option (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs:)
- Stale events after suspend are dropped (packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:)

- Tests guard against panics from stale ids ("invalid SlotMap key used", "invalid key") and `unreachable!()` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stale_interaction_state.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/animations.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/custom_widget_layout.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stale_node_mapping.rs:); a stale animation entry for a removed animated node is to be skipped safely on the next resolve (tests/blitz-tests/tests/animations.rs:)

- Query APIs return `Result<Option<NodeId>>`; missing elements are `None` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/comment_layout.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/harness_smoke.rs:); unknown fragment targets return `None`/`false` and leave scroll at 0 (tests/blitz-tests/tests/fragment_navigation.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/fragment_navigation.rs:)

- The WPT runner catches per-test panics and converts them to a CRASH result (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:); net handler panics are caught and mapped to `WptNetProviderError::HandlerPanic` with the panic message (wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:); a harness that never reports but had uncaught JS errors yields FAIL with an "Uncaught JS error" subtest, otherwise TIMEOUT (wpt/runner/src/test_runners/harness_test.rs:)
**Panic paths:**

- URL handling: `resolve_url` panics when a URL cannot be resolved against the base URL (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); `set_base_url` unwraps `Url::parse` (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); `launch_url` panics on an invalid URL and unwraps the fetch result and UTF-8 decoding (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:)

- Network: building the reqwest client (`unwrap`), resolving the cache directory (`expect`), acquiring the per-host semaphore (`expect`), and reading a multipart form file (`expect`) (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:)

- Parsing: the HTML, XML and fragment parse drivers `unwrap` their `read_from` result (packages/blitz-html/src/html_sink.rs:; packages/blitz-html/src/html_sink.rs:; packages/blitz-html/src/html_sink.rs:); image decoding uses `.expect("IO errors impossible with Cursor")` (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:)

- DOM internals: mutex locks on the font context are `.unwrap()`ed (packages/blitz-dom/src/font_metrics.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:); time reads go through the document's `Clock` and carry no epoch `unwrap` (packages/blitz-dom/src/clock.rs:); invariant violations use `expect` with messages (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:); finding a non-anonymous ancestor panics when none exists (packages/blitz-dom/src/traversal.rs:); `universal_accessors`, `layout_data` and `guard` panic when called on node kinds that lack the field (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:); `layout_style()` panics if the node has no computed styles (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:)

- Unimplemented paths: Stylo hooks, twelve dioxus event-data conversions and the accesskit_xplat macOS and Windows adapters for UiKit and WinRt handles reach `todo!`, `unimplemented!` or `panic!`; no physical key code hits a `todo!()`.

- Layout: a table root without styles panics ("Ignoring table because it has no styles") (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/table.rs:); a node flagged table root without a `TableContext` panics (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:); `unreachable!()` is used for states the code treats as impossible (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/inline/layout.rs:); anchor-positioning sizes and non-breadth `fit-content()` track limits hit `unreachable!()` (packages/stylo_taffy/src/convert.rs:; packages/stylo_taffy/src/convert.rs:); painting a node flagged as inline root without inline layout data panics (packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:)

- Debug-only checks: under `debug_assertions`, layout-parent consistency is asserted and a missing child panics (packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:); a `debug_assert` checks that compared nodes share the root (packages/blitz-dom/src/traversal.rs:); ResumeReady arriving before the renderer is ready trips a debug_assert (packages/blitz-shell/src/application.rs:)

- Shell and runtime setup: event loop construction, window creation, Android app setup, the JS runtime's context and extensions, the timer thread, the tokio runtime and the raw window handle `unwrap` or `expect` and panic on failure.

- Dioxus nodes: supported event-data conversions `unwrap` the platform-data downcast (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:); `NodeHandle::node`/`node_mut` panic with "Node does not exist in the Document" (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/events.rs:); `element_to_node_id` unwraps (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/mutation_writer.rs:)

- Apps and examples: rdme unwraps fetch results and UTF-8 decoding (apps/readme/src/main.rs:; apps/readme/src/readme_application.rs:); AnyRender scene capture unwraps archive and file errors (apps/browser/src/capture.rs:); network and file errors in `screenshot` are `unwrap()`ed (examples/screenshot.rs:; examples/screenshot.rs:; examples/screenshot.rs:); GPU setup and rendering failures in `paint_bench` `expect` with messages "No compatible device found", "Failed to create vello renderer", "Failed to create wgpu device", "Failed to render to texture" (examples/paint_bench.rs:; examples/paint_bench.rs:; examples/paint_bench.rs:; examples/paint_bench.rs:; examples/paint_bench.rs:); `preact_script` panics with `could not resolve {raw_path}: {err}` and `could not read {path}: {err}` (examples/preact_script.rs:; examples/preact_script.rs:); `multi_doc` panics on an unknown mode (examples/multi_doc.rs:)

- WPT runner: failure to run `git rev-parse HEAD` panics (wpt/runner/src/report.rs:); a Crash subtest status is `unreachable!()` in report conversion and expectations output (wpt/runner/src/report.rs:; wpt/runner/src/report.rs:); a test-file read error other than invalid UTF-8 panics (wpt/runner/src/test_runners/mod.rs:); the attribute test runner unwraps the node it reads, panicking on a node id that does not resolve (wpt/runner/src/test_runners/attr_test.rs:)

**Error reporting integration:** observed absent — searched: `counter!|histogram!|gauge!|info_span|debug_span|#\[instrument|tracing::span|sentry|opentelemetry` over the 15 s05 files; `tracing|log::|env_logger|sentry|opentelemetry|metrics` over the 61 s12 files.

title: Logging & Monitoring

body: Detail: .andromeda/security-plan-detail/logging-monitoring.md — read whole.
**What is logged:**

- The browser logs successful loads at info with the resolved URL (apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs:); load failures, script fetch failures and JS errors at error (apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs:; apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs:; apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs:); external-browser open failures at error (apps/browser/src/nav.rs:); persistence warnings are prefixed `history_store:` (apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:; apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:; apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:)

- Network logging (feature `tracing`) records the request URL as field `url`, plus `status` or `error` (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:); the cache directory path is logged at info level as field `path` (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:)
- Resource load failures log structured fields `url`, `waiting_nodes`, `error` (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:)
- Asset-fetch logs print the full request with Debug formatting (packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:; packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:; packages/dioxus-native/src/assets.rs:)

- JS console output (log/info/warn/error) goes to the `log` crate at debug level, target `js_console`, keeping stdout/stderr clean (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime.rs:); with the `tracing` feature, uncaught JS errors are logged with `tracing::error!` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/events.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:)
- A devtools hover-highlight mode logs the clicked node instead of handling the click (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:)

- WPT runner: WPT_DIR value (info) and its absence (error) (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:); glob failure (error) (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:); net load errors with URL and path at warn, pending requests at debug (wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:; wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:; wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:; wpt/runner/src/net_provider.rs:); skips — quarantined (debug), non-UTF-8 (warn), unsupported testdriver (debug), unresolvable/unreadable refs (warn) (wpt/runner/src/test_runners/mod.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/mod.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/harness_test.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/ref_test.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/ref_test.rs:; wpt/runner/src/test_runners/ref_test.rs:)

- CI publish sets `CARGO_LOG: info` and runs `dx bundle --verbose --trace`, on upstream `DioxusLabs/blitz` only — the `release-cli` job is repository-guarded (.github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:; .github/workflows/publish-browser.yml:)
**Log format and backends:**

- Engine crates log through the `tracing` crate behind a `tracing` feature (packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:); the macros compile only with that feature (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_cursor_icon.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/events/ime.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/util.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/convert_events.rs:; packages/blitz-paint/src/render/background.rs:; packages/blitz-paint/src/render/mask.rs:)

- dioxus-native's `tracing` feature also turns on tracing in dioxus-native-dom, blitz-shell, blitz-dom, blitz-html and blitz-net (packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:; packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml:)
- The WPT runner's logger is `env_logger::init()` (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:)

- escher's own sink: both seven_guis binaries install `escher_telemetry::init`, a stderr-only allowlist subscriber — an engine target only seven allowlisted fields, the rest `[redacted]`; an `escher_` target all but eleven content-named fields; any other target dropped whole at every level, spans by the same rule; its reach is that sink only: upstream's `fmt::init()` subscribers, `env_logger` and the panic hook stay unscrubbed, and an allowlisted `log.file` can still carry a host path.

- Stdout output: examples print through `println!` and `eprintln!`; `escher-session` writes one uncoloured JSON line per command on stdout, its `mcp` role JSON-RPC lines only, usage and error messages on stderr, and no line holds anything the caller typed but the `mcp` role's echoed request `id`; debug dumps, timings and test diagnostics also go to stdout.
- Console logging calls are observed absent in the fixtures — searched: `console\.` over the 21 s02 files

- The agent-run test contract (`scripts/agent-run.sh`) logs harness metadata only: its JSON-line events in `target/agent-run/events.jsonl` carry no content-named field (`event ts outcome cargo_exit head selection files file test passed failed ignored booted boot_ts run state`) and no captured test output or panic text; its `target/agent-run/run.log` holds the raw cargo/libtest output, unscrubbed like `target/ci-logs/`, never printed by `logs`, gitignored under `target/` (scripts/agent-run.sh:; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-stand-test-contract/report.md — a live `logs` read held 0 scrub-set keys)

- The cold-agent pipe (`scripts/cold-agent.sh`) logs run metadata only: its events and verdict carry counts, booleans and closed words, never transcript text, a tool argument or answer, a reply or the check; its server log, check, raw transcript and the live child's kept checks under `target/cold-agent/record/` are never printed, the transcript unscrubbed by design and gitignored, each committed copy's host paths masked.

No served network API exists — no served TCP or UDP port: two `blitz-net` tests each call `std::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")` in the crate's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, served by no binary, reached by no caller, so no crossing, registered as test-only (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:), as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph/report.md; the one listener is local: the driver session's Unix-domain socket `{state_dir}/session.sock`, bound at one site since 2026-10-07-driver-session and serving the lifecycle (`hello`, `stop`) and, since 2026-10-10-driver-cli, driver calls and their answers (`call`, wire `v3` since 2026-10-19-session-recording, its replies including the fixed `ok v3 recording-failed`) (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:; its row is below). The net provider fetches arbitrary `http(s)` URLs through reqwest, reads `file:` URLs from local disk, and decodes `data:` URLs (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:). The parser ingests HTML and XHTML strings, and parses SVG image data from raw bytes (packages/blitz-html/src/html_document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/svg.rs:).   - **Trust boundary:** Iframe nesting depth is limited to guard against infinitely recursive self-embedding pages (packages/blitz-dom/src/iframe.rs:). `@import` nesting depth is limited to prevent unbounded recursion, e.g. an import URL that grows geometrically per level (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:). Stale iframe responses (iframe removed or re-navigated since the request) are discarded by request id (packages/blitz-dom/src/iframe.rs:). ## 2026-10-07-driver-session — the driver session socket: threat vector, access, input rows
**Section:** §Threat Model Summary → Attack surface (new vector: local IPC) · §Authentication & Authorization (new row) · §Input Validation (four new rows: session socket · state directory · label · `escher-session` argv) · §API Security (lead · new control row) · §Secret Management → Environment values read · §Dependency Security → Pinning (citations)
**Change:**
- API Security lead: was "No served API surface exists … listeners are observed absent"; now no served network API and no TCP or UDP port, with one local listener — the driver session's Unix-domain socket `session.sock`, lifecycle messages only.
- Access: no handshake, token or peer-credential check; the state directory is created `0700`, one open to group or others is refused (`StateDirNotPrivate`), the socket is `0600` — the owning user only.
- Validation: requests parsed against a closed grammar (`hello v1`, `stop v1`), bounded at 64 bytes, a 2 s read and write bound, refusals and broken connections changing nothing; replies carry a pid, the label and a count only; the label is 1-32 bytes of `a-z0-9-`, checked before the boot; the binary's argv is closed (two arguments, four tasks) and exits 2 before anything boots; `stop` removes the socket file and the directory, nothing else.
- Environment: two build-time `env!` values in the session checks; the library and the binary read no env var beyond `RUST_LOG`.
- Citations: root `Cargo.toml:104; :114` → `:106; :116`; the blitz-tests dev-dependency range → `:15-40`.
**Why:** a new listener and a new input surface are a security-plan amendment first. A boundary widening, ratified by the founder's own choice (the founder, 2026-10-07, relayed verbatim). Standing: the wire carries nothing of the screen; a command that carries an id, a name, a value, snapshot text or a diff reopens the crossing question.

## 2026-10-07-command-and-refusal-schema — a driver call is validated before anything runs; a refusal holds nothing of the call
**Section:** §Input Validation (new row: Driver command schema) · §API Security (the "Settle and loads in flight" row) · §Error Handling → Error format (typed errors)
**Change:**
- §Input Validation gains the row "Driver command schema (escher-driver)": `validate` checks a caller-built call against a closed table of five verbs and five argument kinds with bounds (`id` 1 to 1024 bytes, `text` 0 to 4096, `key` one of twelve names, `flag`, `milliseconds` 1 to 60000) and returns a typed `Command` or a `Refusal`, one answer per call in a fixed order; no `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!` or index on what a call supplies; no clock read; no `Session` in its signature, so a refused call changes nothing. Held in process: not yet an external-input surface. `Command`, `Call` and `ArgValue` print an id and typed text under `Debug`; nothing prints, logs or fields them.

Its stack reference reads `blitz-test-harness · escher-driver`.
- §Error Handling gains the `Refusal` bullet: a closed set of eight causes with fixed non-empty texts holding no path, a `Fault` carrying at most the schema's own argument name, no `String` field in `Cause`, `Fault` or `Refusal`.
**Why:** the chunk built the check every later driver surface's input passes through. That no driver command waits on a load is the operator's answer, given at the plan's forks on 2026-10-07. ## 2026-10-13-range-input-interaction — the range input row, a boundary widening ratified
**Section:** §Input Validation (a new `Markup attributes` row for `input type="range"`; the `disabled` row)
**Change:**
- New row. In every document, the browser app's remote pages included, a range input holds a current value apart from its `value` attribute.
  - `min`, `max`, `step` and `value` are read through `parse_float`, the HTML floating-point rules: a parse error, NaN or an infinity reads absent; `-0` reads `0`.
  - Defaults: `min` 0, `max` 100, `step` 1. A `max` below `min` reads `min`; a step ≤ 0 or unparsable reads 1; `any` sets no grid. The base is `min`, else `value`, else 0; the default is the overflow-free midpoint.
  - Every seed, write and move is sanitized: clamped, put on the grid with an overflow-free index, rounded to the step's and base's decimals and written shortest round-trip. The value stays finite, bounded and on the grid on degenerate markup (8 unit rows, 7 integration rows).
  - The keys (arrows, `Home`, `End`), a main-button pointerdown by position and a focusing click act only with no `disabled` attribute.
  - One `input` per change. A `value` write re-seeds and a `min`/`max`/`step` write re-sanitizes.
  - No print, log site, `unwrap`, `expect`, panic or env read.
  - The value leaves only as the form entry, the `input` event's value and the snapshot's `value`, a control value inside the ratified carriers. No carrier, verb, field, log field, span or accessibility value or action is added.
- `disabled` row: presence now also gates the range input's key, pointerdown and click arms.
**Why:** a boundary widening, a validated surface admitting a new input class from any document's markup. It was ratified by the founder, never routine, by question dialog in the overseer session, each answer relayed verbatim by the overseer as his chosen option label:
- his ruling of 2026-10-07 «Пусть будет а»;
- his three fork answers of 2026-10-13 «Отдельное текущее значение», «Стрелки + Home/End (Рекомендую)» and «Клик даёт фокус (Рекомендую)»;

## 2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph — a failed load reaches the handler and ends the wait
**Section:** §API Security (api-security.md: Settle and loads in flight); §Error Handling (security-plan.md: Internal logging; error-handling.md: a new group, Failed load answered through the handler)
**Change:**
- Settle and loads in flight gains: a failed load ends the wait. `CountedHandler` forwards `NetHandler::error`, so a failed stylesheet reads no `NotSettled(Loads)` for good on a harness document or on the driver, and `settle_waiting` returns where it would otherwise have run to `LOAD_WAIT`.
- New row: `NetHandler::error` stands on the public trait, a default that does nothing, so a wrapping implementer that does not forward it compiles and drops the failure silently; `ResourceHandler<StylesheetHandler>::error` responds `Err(error)`, so `pending_critical_resources` loses the request and a failed, empty or non-CSS stylesheet does not block render.
- The master's `NetProvider::fetch` line: was a failed fetch logged when tracing is enabled and otherwise discarded, the handler not called on error; now logged when tracing is enabled and handed to the handler through `NetHandler::error`, a default that does nothing, with or without tracing.
- The master's failed-loads line gains: a failed stylesheet's request leaves `pending_critical_resources`, so it blocks no render.
**Why:** `f6edb9701`, one of the twelve commits the founder took by his answer to fork F2, option A (2026-11-01, by dialog in the overseer session, relayed verbatim by the operator), adds the method and has `blitz-net`'s error arm call it, which makes the old master claim false. title: Motion (calibrated to expression level `unrecorded`)

body: Detail: .andromeda/design-system-detail/motion.md — read whole.

**Expression level:**
> NO RECORDED INTENT
**This project's values:**

A programmatic into-view scroll never animates a nested scrolling box: every scrolling box holding its target is written at once, innermost first, whatever behaviour was asked, and the requested behaviour, `Smooth` included, applies to the viewport alone; the driver's `scroll` is instant in every box and in the viewport; into view on a row of an open select list writes that list's own scroll at once, moving no other box and no viewport.
**Animation runtime:**

A harness settle answers every member of the document's animating set the same way — none holds it open, none is waited on or advanced: it returns `Settled`, `animating` reading the document's animating flag.

The test harness drives animation from the `VirtualClock` its documents read, and settle reads animation time only through it, never advancing it; the driver's `advance` moves it by exactly its `ms` and, through the step a session's caller hands it, the app's own time together, while `click`, `type` and `press` leave it where it was.

The driver's load wait moves no clock: while an acting step waits on a load in flight, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, the harness's `VirtualClock` stands still, so a timer or an animation does not run during the wait.

`escher-session`, the driver's command line, and its `mcp` role are surfaces an agent reads, not a person: stdout holds only JSON — one line per command (the answer, the refusal or a session error's object), or newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 lines — never colour or an ESC byte, and no code tests for a terminal, so the output is the same piped or not; the command line's exit status carries the class (`0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error), and an `mcp` `Err` ending exits `3`.

title: IA notes

body: - Each document starts with the fixed skeleton `<html><head></head><body><main id="main"></main></body></html>` and the app mounts into `main` (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:)
- Arbitrary `index.html` templates are not supported (a TODO) (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:)
- Head elements (title, meta, script, style, link) are appended to `<head>`, with optional text contents (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:)
- Launch config carries `stylesheets` and `base_url` (packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz/src/lib.rs:)

- The viewport is the window surface minus safe-area insets, while the render surface covers the whole window including the safe area (packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:)
- Pointer client coordinates subtract the safe-area left/top insets and page coordinates add viewport scroll (packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:)

- The document element is the scrolling element; `window.scrollTo`/`scrollBy` scroll the root element (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/document.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/window.rs:)
- The root element's `clientWidth`/`clientHeight` are viewport size minus scrollbar size (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/element/geometry.rs:)
- Fixed-position children of the root element are not scrolled with the viewport (packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:)

- **blitz-dom covered behaviours:** mutation, invalidation, hover, `@font-face` loading and mapping, the changed set, the font reading, the text extent reader, the `select` model, single and `multiple`, with `optgroup` and a single select's painted list, and hit testing past a dropped node, each read by blitz-dom unit tests or blitz-tests checks; `layout_as_text_input` has no unit test of its own; the text extent's stated limits are asserted by blitz-tests' `text_extent` and the select's by `select_interaction` and `stand_act_select`, and its list's by `select_popup`, `select_popup_painted` and `stand_act_popup`; the process-wide `Parallel` traversal lock is asserted by no check; `:open` matching a `details` or `dialog` carrying `open` is read by blitz-tests' `open_state`

- **blitz-dom (style bridge):** `stylo_to_parley.rs` holds nine unit tests of font feature mapping (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_parley.rs:); `util.rs` holds seven SVG parsing tests compiled only with the `svg` feature (packages/blitz-dom/src/util.rs:); `stylo.rs` holds two `#[test]` functions whose bodies are entirely commented out (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:)

- **blitz-html:** one test parses a full HTML document through `DocumentHtmlParser` (packages/blitz-html/src/html_sink.rs:)

- **blitz-net:** its `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` pins a load's delivery — `delivers_successful_and_empty_responses`, `delivers_network_and_bad_url_errors` and `http_error_body_is_not_delivered_as_css`, the last two each over a test-only `TcpListener::bind` on `127.0.0.1:0`, served by no binary and reached by no caller (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:); its `file:` read, which since the 2026-10-10 upstream merge goes through `Url::to_file_path` off wasm, has no test named for it (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:) — as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph/report.md

- **escher-telemetry:** inline unit tests in `format.rs` of the scrub decision, the bridged `log` record, the outside-target drop and the closed span, and one in `lib.rs` of the `service_identity!()` expansion; its process-global behaviours are the `telemetry_*` integration files

- **blitz-vibey-script:** tests/dom.rs covers the JS DOM APIs, tests/selection.rs the script Selection API, tests/url_search_params.rs the global `URLSearchParams` and `URL.prototype.searchParams`, and tests/preact.rs runs the vendored Preact TodoMVC example headlessly; a test of the `innerText` / `outerText` getters is observed absent

- **dioxus-native-dom:** unit tests of the snapshot builder, its text form, its parts and its diff, the stable element id, the actionable-key check, the bridge, the mutation writer and the document's events; the two limits of the boolean model — a mixed toggle reads unpressed, a grammar or spelling error reads invalid — are pinned here and at the engine only
