title: 3. Test Harness Contract
body:
## 3. Test Harness Contract

**Runners and invocation:**

- **WPT in CI:** invoked as `cargo build -rp wpt` then `cargo run -rp wpt css svg`, producing `./wpt/output/wptreport.json` (.github/workflows/wpt.yml:53-58); the `wpt` cli provides `calc-scores` and `diff --format json` (.github/workflows/wpt.yml:69-80)
- **WPT runner CLI:** `WPT_DIR` env var, optional suite arguments, `--verbose`/`-v`, `--run-quarantined`, `--list` (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:240-250; wpt/runner/src/main.rs:461-479)
- **WPT outputs:** `wpt_expectations.txt` and `wptreport.json` in the output directory (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:832-847)
- **WPT status set:** PASS, FAIL, TIMEOUT, SKIP, CRASH (wpt/runner/src/main.rs:104-122)
- **Python script tests:** the test file states it runs with `python3 -m unittest discover .github/scripts` (.github/scripts/test_wpt_diff_to_pr.py:2)
- **Rust tests:** the standard built-in harness — `#[cfg(test)]` modules with `#[test]` functions and `assert!`/`assert_eq!` (packages/blitz-dom/src/net.rs:606-618; packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_to_parley.rs:550-564; packages/blitz-dom/src/util.rs:191-200; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/list.rs:185-204; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/scrollbar.rs:228-236; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1754-1761), with `#[tokio::test]` for async worker tests (apps/browser/src/url_suggestions.rs:415; apps/browser/src/url_suggestions.rs:551)
- **Feature gating:** SVG tests are gated on both `test` and the `svg` feature (packages/blitz-dom/src/util.rs:180)
- **Third-party test frameworks:** observed absent · searched: `proptest|insta::|criterion|mock` over the 15 files of slice s05

**blitz-test-harness (`Harness`):**

- **Construction:** from_html, from_html_with, from_component, from_vdom, wrap; constructors pump once, wrap does not (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:59-92). `Harness::from_html(html)` and `Harness::from_html_with(html, HarnessOptions)` build an HTML-backed harness; `Harness::from_component(fn)` and `Harness::from_vdom(vdom, options)` build Dioxus-backed ones (tests/blitz-tests/tests/harness_smoke.rs:10; tests/blitz-tests/tests/pointer_events.rs:8-17; tests/blitz-tests/tests/harness_smoke.rs:104; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stale_node_mapping.rs:49-56)
- **Core:** into_inner, base, base_mut, time, pump, tick, dispatch, dispatch_recorded, set_viewport_size (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:94-184)
- **Pump semantics:** pump polls the document with no waker context and resolves at the harness time; dispatch and dispatch_recorded do not pump (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/harness.rs:113-138); `pump()` applies pending changes after a mutation through `base_mut().mutate()` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/dir_attribute.rs:72-79; tests/blitz-tests/tests/oof_dynamic_cb.rs:37-43)
- **Recorded dispatch:** `dispatch_recorded([UiEvent, ...])` returns the list of dispatched event names (tests/blitz-tests/tests/touch_events.rs:40-44)
- **Input helpers:** click, click_at, mouse_down_at, mouse_up_at, move_mouse_to, drag, tap, tap_at, touch_down, touch_move, touch_up, wheel_at, press, press_with, type_text, ime — each pumps after dispatch (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:95-232); synthesized pointer events set page, screen and client coordinates to the same values (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:18-27); key_event uses Code::Unidentified and Location::Standard and fills text only for pressed character keys (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/input.rs:75-93); the crate exports a `pointer_event(id, x, y, button, buttons, mods)` builder (tests/blitz-tests/tests/touch_events.rs:6; tests/blitz-tests/tests/touch_events.rs:12-21)
- **Inspection helpers:** query, node, query_all, layout_rect, layout_rect_of, center_of, text_content, attr, hit, hit_node, focused, hovered, dom_string (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/inspect.rs:26-131); `layout_rect(selector)` returns a rect with `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`; `center_of` returns an `(x, y)` tuple (tests/blitz-tests/tests/harness_smoke.rs:16-21)

**Crate-local test helpers:**

- **apps/browser:** `drive_worker` queues messages, drops the sender, captures publications, and bounds the run with a 2-second timeout (apps/browser/src/url_suggestions.rs:364-388); `make_conn` opens an in-memory sqlite connection and migrates it to latest (apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:322-326)
- **blitz-dom node tests:** DOM tests construct `BaseDocument::new(DocumentConfig::default())` and create nodes with `create_node` (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1743-1752); text-input tests build a `TextInputData` laid out at scale 1.0 with fresh parley `FontContext`/`LayoutContext` (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs:963-974)
- **blitz-vibey-script:** `doc_from_html` constructs with the default `DocumentConfig` and calls `execute_scripts`; `text_of_selector` reads text content (packages/blitz-vibey-script/tests/dom.rs:8-21); preact helpers: load_todomvc, resolve, query, query_all, text_of, enter_key, click, add_todo (packages/blitz-vibey-script/tests/preact.rs:16-100); virtual time and `without_timer_thread` are intended for embedders driving timers manually, e.g. test runners (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/clock.rs:10-14; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:108-133); dev-dependency blitz-dom enables `system-fonts` so text inputs shape real text in the selection tests (packages/blitz-vibey-script/Cargo.toml:42-48)
- **dioxus-native-dom:** the tests use the `dioxus` crate as a dev-dependency (packages/dioxus-native-dom/Cargo.toml:43-44; packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:370); the document test builds a `DioxusDocument` with `DocumentConfig::default()`, calls `initial_build`, and drives updates with `mark_dirty` and `poll(None)` (packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/dioxus_document.rs:394-404)

> NOT YET MEASURED — the reading reached the test runners and the in-process harness only; no product boot, status, cleanup or logs command, status endpoint shape, log format, PID file or test-data bootstrap mechanism of a 5-command contract was gathered

title: 2. Telemetry Strategy

body: Detail: .andromeda/obs-plan-detail/telemetry-strategy.md — read whole.
**Telemetry mechanism (current truth):**

- Telemetry is the `tracing` crate's event macros and, in escher-driver, two span macros (`command` and `tool_call`, §4), compiled into the engine and upstream crates only with the `tracing` cargo feature; escher-telemetry and escher-driver take `tracing` with no feature, so the startup and panic events and the command span are always compiled into the seven_guis package's two native binaries, `seven_guis_native` and `escher-session`, whose engine features stay off in a package-alone build.
- Each feature-gated `tracing` call has a no-op path when the feature is off (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:)
- Each blitz-dom log site is compiled only with `#[cfg(feature = "tracing")]` (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:)
- The blitz-dom crate root comment lists a `tracing` feature that "Enables tracing support", under a TODO to document features (packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:)

- `tracing` is the only telemetry dependency in blitz-paint and blitz-shell, where it is optional (packages/blitz-paint/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-paint/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml:)

- `tracing` is an optional dependency of blitz-net and blitz-html, enabled only by the `tracing` feature (packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-net/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-html/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz-html/Cargo.toml:)
**Feature wiring:**
- The browser `tracing` feature enables tracing in dioxus-native, blitz-html, blitz-net, blitz-paint and pulls in tracing-subscriber (apps/browser/Cargo.toml:)
- rdme's `tracing` feature enables it in blitz-shell, blitz-net, blitz-html (apps/readme/Cargo.toml:)
- `tracing` is a default feature of blitz and forwards to blitz-shell, blitz-html and blitz-net (packages/blitz/Cargo.toml:; packages/blitz/Cargo.toml:)

- By invocation: a build that resolves the whole workspace (`cargo test --workspace`, `ci-leg.sh fast`, CI's test leg) turns `blitz-dom/tracing` on, while `cargo test -p blitz-tests` and a `-p seven_guis` build leave it off; so under the workspace build a test child that installs escher's sink at `info` also receives engine events (test-plan §9 → Engine features by runner).
- blitz-vibey-script's `tracing` feature is off by default and also enables `blitz-dom/tracing` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/Cargo.toml:)
- dioxus-native's `tracing` feature turns on tracing across dioxus-native-dom and the blitz crates (packages/dioxus-native/Cargo.toml:)

- `log-frame-times` and `log-phase-times` features forward to renderer and DOM crates (apps/browser/Cargo.toml:; apps/readme/Cargo.toml:; examples/todomvc/Cargo.toml:; examples/counter/Cargo.toml:)

- blitz-dom's `log-phase-times` enables `debug_timer/enable` (packages/blitz-dom/Cargo.toml:)
**Absent:**

- Telemetry backends observed absent over the CI and build files, telemetry, tracing or logging frameworks over the reading's examples and test crate slices, and tracing or metrics libraries over its wpt runner slice, each search standing for its slice.

**Logging stack (subscriber installation):**

- `seven_guis_native` (the windowed stand binary) installs `escher_telemetry::init(escher_telemetry::service_identity!())` in the native `main` before `dioxus_native::launch`, reporting an `Err` with `eprintln!` and continuing (examples/seven_guis/src/main.rs:): a global `Registry` with an `EnvFilter` from `RUST_LOG` (default `warn`) and one non-ANSI fmt layer — stated once, in the private `sink_layer`, with `with_span_events(FmtSpan::CLOSE)` and the crate-private field formatter `SpanFields` — that prints each event and, since 2026-10-07-driver-command-spans, each closed span through the escher formatter (§6 Log format), writing to stderr only, plus the `tracing_log::LogTracer` bridge for `log` records (packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:; packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:)

- `escher-session` (the driver's command line and, in its host role, the headless session host; the second binary of the seven_guis package) installs the same `escher_telemetry::init(escher_telemetry::service_identity!())` first thing in its native `main` — before argv is read and before anything boots — reporting an `Err` with `eprintln!` and continuing; the same subscriber, stderr only; since 2026-10-10-driver-cli `main` then hands argv, the stand's six slugs (`counter` · `flight-booker` · `timer` · `crud` · `cells` · `load`, its private `Served` table, the usage line's `apps:` and the MCP `start` tool's `enum` following as the program's own fixed text) and the stand's boot to `escher_driver::command_line`, which installs no subscriber, reads no environment variable and writes each command's answer, refusal or session-error object as one uncoloured line of JSON on stdout — an answer, never a log line: the sink still writes to stderr only, and the host role ends quiet; since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the reader takes the first word `mcp` as a role, alone or with one `--record <dir>`, whose directory is checked before `serve_mcp` serves (a refusal: status 3, its fixed message on stderr, stdout empty), and `run` hands it to `serve_mcp(stdin, stdout, apps, boot, IDLE_EXPIRY)`, which installs no subscriber and reads no environment variable, its stdout newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol lines only, written by the crate's hand writer and never by the sink, its end writing nothing on stdout — status 0 on `Ok`, 3 with the error's fixed message on stderr on `Err` — the role a third reach of the same install in the same `main`; `init` has two install sites (packages/escher-driver/src/cli.rs:; examples/seven_guis/src/session_host.rs:; examples/seven_guis/Cargo.toml:; as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-07-driver-session/report.md)

title: 6. Log Coverage

body: Detail: .andromeda/obs-plan-detail/log-coverage.md — read whole.
**Log format (escher's sink):**

- One line per printed event and one per closed span, on stderr, no ANSI. An event's line: `{RFC 3339 UTC time} {LEVEL} {target} service.name={name} service.version={version} {field}={value}…`; newlines and carriage returns in values escaped as `\n` / `\r`, string values Debug-quoted; a bridged `log` record printed under its `log.target`, that field itself omitted; every field passes the §8 scrub; an event from a target outside the sink's allowlist (§8 → Scrubbing) prints nothing at all — not an empty line — a bridged record judged by its `log.target` (packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs:)

- A closed span's line, the sink's second record class, is written for each closed span whose target the allowlist admits, and no line when a span is created, recorded to, entered or exited: `{time} {LEVEL} {target} service.name=… service.version=… span={the span's name}`, then the span's own fields in the order recorded, then `message`, `time.busy` and `time.idle`; every pair passes the §8 scrub; an event's line is unchanged inside a span.

- Per-module levels come from `RUST_LOG` through `EnvFilter`, defaulting to `warn` when unset or unparsable (packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:); a directive that names a target outside the sink's allowlist (`style=trace`) lets its records past the filter and the formatter still drops them — the formatter is the last thing a record meets (tests/blitz-tests/tests/telemetry_drop.rs:)
**Log format (the agent-run harness, §3):**

- One JSON object per line on stdout, the same lines appended to `target/agent-run/events.jsonl` (recreated by `boot`, removed by `cleanup`): `boot {ts, outcome, cargo_exit, head}` · `run.start {ts, selection, files}` · `test {file, test, outcome}` · `run.end {ts, selection, passed, failed, ignored, cargo_exit, outcome}`; `status {booted, boot_ts, head, run}` and `cleanup {outcome}` are printed only (scripts/agent-run.sh:)

- One `test` event per libtest result line, `file` the target binary's stem with its hash stripped or `doc:{crate}`; nothing between a `failures:` line and the next `test result:` is read, so captured stdout and panic text never reach an event; the raw cargo output goes to `target/agent-run/run.log`, truncated at each run's start and never printed (scripts/agent-run.sh:; scripts/agent-run.sh:)
**Log format (the cold-agent pipe, §3):**

- One JSON object per line on stdout, the same lines appended to `target/cold-agent/events.jsonl` (recreated by `run`, removed by `cleanup`): `run.start {ts, task}` · `run.end {every verdict field}`; `status {the verdict}` or `status {outcome: "none"}` (exit 3) and `cleanup {outcome: "done"}` are printed only (scripts/cold-agent.sh:)

- The verdict fields are each a count, a boolean or a closed word — no transcript text, tool argument, tool answer, reply or check; `counts_agree` ties the server's span lines to the transcript and `wrong_calls` counts refused, error and foreign tool uses and permission denials; `lint_calls` · `screenshot_calls` · `advance_calls` count the accepted `tool_call` span lines of each counted verb, `part_reads` the paged snapshot reads, `recorded_sessions` and `recording_kept` the live child's kept checks, and `wrong_calls` decides against `wrong_call_bar_pct` (5), the reasons adding `capability-unused` · `recording-not-kept` · `wrong-calls-over-bar` (`wrong_calls × 100 > 5 × tool_calls`) after `task-unmet` and before the check's.

- The server log (since 2026-10-15-cold-agent-test, the stub's call log retired with the stub): the live escher server child's stderr at `RUST_LOG=info` goes to `target/cold-agent/server.log` — escher's sink lines, one closed `tool_call` span per tool call (§6, escher-driver) — which the pipe reads only to count ` span="tool_call" ` lines, their ` ending="refused" ` / ` ending="error" ` and the accepted lines of each counted verb, `lint` · `screenshot` · `advance` (`span_counts`), never printing or copying it; the live child runs `mcp --record` into `target/cold-agent/record/` (made `mkdir -m 700`), the replay children without `--record` (scripts/cold-agent.sh:)

- The client's raw stream-json goes to `target/cold-agent/transcript.jsonl` and its stderr to `client.log`, the escher server's stderr to `server.log` (counted by span name only) the agent's check, written as parsed (`json.dump`, `indent=2`), to `check.json` and the live session's kept checks to `target/cold-agent/record/`; none is printed or copied (scripts/cold-agent.sh:)
> NOT YET MEASURED — a log JSON schema, a log-file sink and a rotation policy for escher's own sink: the reading recorded none of them
**Logged events (current truth):**
- **apps/browser** — document loads log at info and error, script prefetch failures and JS errors at error, and urlbar parse failures, persistence failures and dropped history writes at warn.

- **examples** — wasm_hello logs at info and example output uses `println!`/`eprintln!`, except `seven_guis_native` and `escher-session`, which log through escher-telemetry; `escher-session`'s own lines are its one `eprintln!` and the endings its command line writes, the `mcp` role writing protocol lines only on stdout; every diagnostic is a fixed string holding no path, label, id or value, and no ending holds anything the caller typed.

- **escher-telemetry (in `seven_guis_native` and `escher-session`)**
  - info at target `escher_telemetry`, message `telemetry installed`, once per successful init — no argv, path or URL (packages/escher-telemetry/src/lib.rs:)
  - ERROR at target `escher_telemetry::panic`, message `panic`, fields `panic.file`, `panic.line`, `panic.column`, `panic.payload` (redacted), once per panic (packages/escher-telemetry/src/panic.rs:)

- **escher-driver (in a process that installs escher's sink at `info` or below)** — one closed-span line per call to `Session::run`, `span="command"` with its recorded fields, and one per MCP tool call, `span="tool_call"` with `tool` and `ending`, each INFO at target `escher_driver`, closed words, bools and counts only — no shot byte, lint finding, part number or text; no line at the default `warn`; `seven_guis_native` runs none.

- **Engine, test and tool emitters** — blitz-dom, blitz-net, blitz-html, blitz-shell, blitz-paint, blitz, blitz-vibey-script, dioxus-native, dioxus-native-dom, tests/blitz-tests, wpt/runner and the CI publish builds: each one's log sites by level, message and field, and blitz-dom's `println!` dumps.

**Scrubbing:**

- escher's own sink applies an allowlist of targets in its formatter, three outcomes: an engine target (`ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES`) prints only the safe fields, the rest `[redacted]`; an `escher_` target (`ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES`) prints every field but the content-named set, which is redacted; any other target is dropped whole before anything is written, at every level and whatever `RUST_LOG` names; a closed span's line is judged pair by pair by the same rule; no engine call site is edited.
- The value of a content-named span field is never stored — its `[redacted]` marker is written at print time — and every other span field's value is held in process memory until the span closes.

- Its reach is that sink, installed by the two binaries of the seven_guis package: engine events reach it only when an engine `tracing` feature is on, and a record from any target outside the two prefix sets is dropped — the cost that a third-party WARN or ERROR never reaches stderr, at any setting; the upstream apps' `fmt::init()` stdout subscribers and the WPT runner's `env_logger` stay unscrubbed.

- The agent-run harness log (§3) sits outside that sink and carries no user content: its events hold only `event`, `ts`, `outcome`, `cargo_exit`, `head`, `selection`, `files`, `file`, `test`, `passed`, `failed`, `ignored`, `booted`, `boot_ts`, `run`, `state` — none in the content-named set — and no captured test output; its `target/agent-run/run.log` is raw cargo/libtest output, unscrubbed by design like `target/ci-logs/`, never printed by `logs` and gitignored under `target/` (as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-06-stand-test-contract/report.md — a live `logs` read held 0 scrub-set keys)

- The cold-agent pipe log sits outside that sink and carries no user content: no event or verdict key is content-named and no transcript text, tool argument, answer, reply or check enters an event or the verdict; `server.log` is counted by span name, never printed; `transcript.jsonl` — raw model output and tool I/O — carries the stand's screens (ids, accessible names, control values; on the live run of six apps also Cells' contents, the flight booker's select options and value, a lint's findings and a shot) to the model provider by design and holds host paths, unscrubbed, never printed, gitignored under `target/`; the live session's kept checks under the owner-only `target/cold-agent/record/` hold its calls and answers at rest, never printed, copied or committed.

## 2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap — escher-telemetry: stderr subscriber, identity, line format, chaining panic hook, allowlist scrub
**Section:** §1 Instrumentation scope · §2 Telemetry mechanism · §3 Logging stack · §3 Service identity and line format · §3 → Bootstrap phases (key file) · §6 Log format · §6 Logged events · §6 Absent · §7 Panic hooks · §8 Values logged as-is · §8 Scrubbing · every section citing `Cargo.toml` or `examples/seven_guis` lines
**Change:**
- §3 Logging stack: was `fmt::init()` as the native install; now `seven_guis_native` calls `escher_telemetry::init` (Registry + `EnvFilter` from `RUST_LOG`, default `warn`, + one non-ANSI fmt layer, stderr only, `LogTracer` bridge; an `Err` is `eprintln!`ed), and `fmt::init()` is the upstream apps' stdout install.
- §3: service identity measured — `service.name` / `service.version` from the binary's `CARGO_PKG_*`; the marker keeps product mode, a JSON schema, log file, snapshot, trace context, heartbeat.
- §6: the one-line text format and `RUST_LOG` levels; events `telemetry installed` (info, `escher_telemetry`) and `panic` (ERROR, `escher_telemetry::panic`); the examples slice no longer `println!`-only.
- §2 / §1: tracing compiled only with the `tracing` feature is the engine and upstream crates' rule — escher-telemetry is ungated; §1 lists tracing-log and the escher-telemetry entity.
- §7: the chaining native hook (logs, then the previous hook; std still prints the raw message).
- §8: was "Scrubbing (absent)"; now the allowlist scrub — engine prefixes `blitz`, `dioxus_native`, `stylo_taffy`, `accesskit_xplat`, `debug_timer`, `js_console` print only `node_id`, `status`, `waiting_nodes`, `property`, `log.module_path`, `log.file`, `log.line`; `url`, `href`, `src`, `html`, `text`, `value`, `attrs`, `path`, `request`, `error`, `panic.payload` redacted everywhere — reaching escher's sink only; the slice search records kept; residue as-is: the raw panic message, `log.file` host paths.
- Bootstrap phases: `pii-scrubbing-wire` discharged for escher's sink, open for the upstream sinks; `otel-sdk-install` open, the opt-in export carried to "Driver command spans".
- 7 `file:line` citations re-pointed.
**Why:** the telemetry bootstrap chunk shipped the bootstrap; OTel export was deferred at P4 by the overseer delegate under the founder's standing delegation of technical forks (egress + credential path), provisional on the founder's word.

## 2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph — a failed load reaches its handler, and where its error text stops
**Section:** §7 Error Capture & Reporting (obs-plan.md: Error classes captured; error-capture-reporting.md: a new `values · errors` group after the absence group); §6 Log Coverage (log-coverage.md: the blitz-dom and blitz-net values); §8 PII Scrubbing & Compliance (pii-scrubbing-compliance.md: the sink's allowlist group)
**Change:**
- §7's blitz-net class: was logged and not propagated to the handler; now logged and handed to the handler through `NetHandler::error`, a default that does nothing unless the handler overrides it; a stylesheet's handler responds `Err(error)`, so `pending_critical_resources` loses the request, the error text stopping in `ResourceLoadResponse` and the `Resource load failed` line.
- error-capture-reporting.md takes three values. blitz-dom: a failed stylesheet is captured as a typed answer, `ResourceHandler<StylesheetHandler>::error` responding `Err(error)`, and a failed, empty or non-CSS stylesheet stops blocking render. blitz-traits: `NetHandler::error` is a public trait method with a do-nothing default, so a handler without an override drops the error; blitz-test-harness's `CountedHandler` forwards it. blitz-net: the error arm calls `handler.error(url, e.to_string())`; no log site of its own, the standing `Error fetching` and `Resource load failed` lines reporting it.
- §6 takes two no-site lines: a failed stylesheet reaches the resource-load-failed line, and a bad `href` starts no load, so it reaches no fetch or load line; the arm that logs `Error fetching` also calls `handler.error`, then the waker.
- §8 and the blitz-net value: `url` and `error` are in escher-telemetry's scrub set, so on `Resource load failed` the sink prints `waiting_nodes` and every other field, the message included, `[redacted]`; no other carrier takes the text.
**Why:** The take's `f6edb9701` puts `NetHandler::error` on the public trait and has blitz-net's error arm call it, which left §7's not-propagated claim false; the standing lines are this path's instrumentation. The report's Schema bullet has the sink printing `waiting_nodes` and the message; main's read of escher-telemetry's formatter at Validate found an engine target's `message` prints `[redacted]`, so the report overstates and the body holds the measured read. Standing trap, from the report: a trait default can hide a take's fix, as this one stopped at `CountedHandler` with no gate reading it; sweep the implementers of a trait a take extends.
**Kept:** §7's `ProviderError` clause stands.

title: 2. A11y Strategy

body: Detail: .andromeda/a11y-plan-detail/a11y-strategy.md — read whole.
**Accessibility tree lifecycle:**

- The accessibility tree is built from the document on InitialTreeRequested and refreshed on change: a poll that takes a non-empty changed set rebuilds the platform tree, both paths through the `Document::accessibility_tree` trait method, so a wrapper's override (DioxusDocument's stable ids) reaches it; proven headlessly on the stand in both layout modes, its windowed witness at the platform adapter owed — owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line that reads `re-carried:0.2.0`, an active assistive technology this version does not reach.

- `changed_nodes` is the engine's changed set, the nodes written since the last `take_changed_nodes`: an in-document mutation, a focus or checked change, a text control's input, a select's changed choice and a single select's list opening or closing mark it — a page scroll or a move that closes a list marks its select through `reconcile_select_list` at the next resolve, a wheel elsewhere through `close_select_list`; node creation, hover, active, scroll and layout do not, save that scroll or move, and a highlight or a wheel move inside a list marks nothing, so a pointer move alone reaches no refresh; a harness settle neither reads nor drains it and a fresh harness document's set is non-empty, so a check reading `has_changes()` as "this step changed something" drains first.
**Role derivation (semantic HTML and ARIA):**
- A node's role comes from its `role` attribute, else from the HTML element mapping, else `Role::Unknown` (packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:)
- A TODO notes that elements with strong native semantics can currently have their role overridden, contrary to WAI-ARIA 1.2 (packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs:)

- The builder writes three states from ARIA state attributes, trimmed and matched in lower case: `aria-selected` → `selected`; `aria-pressed` → `toggled` on all but the five checkable roles, `aria-checked` → `toggled` on those alone; `aria-invalid` → `invalid`; a select's option reads its chosen state; a native checkbox or radio under a checkable role writes `toggled` from its own checked state, reading neither author attribute, and under any other role writes nothing, so `pressed` never begins to read on it — the windowed AT witness owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line that reads `re-carried:0.2.0`, an active assistive technology this version does not reach.

- The builder also holds upstream's six reads — `aria-labelledby` (its targets' text the `label`, outranking a `<label>` and an `aria-label`, accname 2B), `aria-describedby`, `aria-description`, `aria-expanded` (on every element but a single select, which writes its list's open state instead), `aria-disabled` and `aria-level` — still one read per attribute; the description and the new closed values leave only to the platform adapter, which no stand binary builds, so what an assistive technology reads of them is not measured.

title: 5. Keyboard Navigation

body: Detail: .andromeda/a11y-plan-detail/keyboard-navigation.md — read whole.
**Focus order per layout (engine):**

- An element is focusable if it holds a sub-document, or is not inert, is no disabled form control and has `tabindex >= 0` or, with no tabindex, is an `<a>`/`<area>` with `href` or a `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `frame`, `iframe` or `summary`; `disabled` counts by presence on a form control alone; HTML's focus fixup is built, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing. The fixup reads `is_inert()` alone, so a focused control that no longer shows, by `hidden`, `style="display:none"` or CSS alone, keeps focus and takes keys, with no panic; the limit is owned by a `CARRY:` on the entry «A11y re-read».

- Disabled-ness is keyed one way: the `DISABLED`/`ENABLED` state (hence `:disabled`), the pointer gates, Enter and Space activation and focusability read the `disabled` attribute's presence on a `button`, `input`, `select` or `textarea`, so `disabled="false"` and a bare `disabled` on a form control match `:disabled` and are not focusable.
**Focus restoration:**

- A pointer click on a `button` or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button` focuses it, submits the form owner when it is a submit button and ends the walk, and a click on a single `select` focuses it and opens its list or closes one standing, each of two clicks on one point focusing; a click on a row of an open list chooses it, a disabled row changing nothing and leaving the list open and a group header choosing nothing; a press outside the list closes it with no event; a label's click on a bound single select focuses it and opens nothing; a click on a `multiple` select focuses it, a click on a `multiple` select's row focuses the select and acts on the row, and an option of a closed single select takes no click; a disabled form control stops the walk first, a disabled ancestor `div` not; a click on any other element is unchanged — a CRUD row or the list still clears focus.

- Two pointer clicks on one point within 500 ms and 2 px are a double click, read on the document's clock (a harness-built document's `VirtualClock`), each still focusing its target as one click does.
- A click on a range input focuses it and changes no value; a main-button pointerdown on one not disabled sets the value from the hit's fraction of the content box, clamped to [0, 1].
**Keyboard handling (engine and shell):**

- A focused `input type="range"` with no `disabled` attribute steps up on ArrowRight and ArrowUp, down on ArrowLeft and ArrowDown, to its minimum on Home and its maximum on End, every other key doing nothing; its value is held apart from the `value` attribute, sanitized to `[min, max]` on the step grid, and each change fires one `input` event, a move that changes nothing none.

- A focused single-choice `select` that is no disabled form control, its list closed, takes ArrowDown / ArrowUp to the next / previous enabled option, Home / End to the first / last, and a character with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta as typeahead kept for 1 s of the document's clock; Enter, and a Space with no typed text standing, open its list on the chosen option and fire nothing, a disabled, inert, hidden or empty select opening nothing; every other key does nothing; each change dispatches one `input` then one `change`, a key that changes nothing none; with the list open the engine paints it over the page and focus stays on the select, its keys moving the highlight over enabled rows and choosing nothing, Enter and Space choosing the highlighted row and closing, Tab in either direction choosing and closing before focus moves, and Escape closing with the value unchanged and no event, as a second click, a press outside and a page scroll do; a close clears the typed text; an `optgroup`'s options are the select's own in tree order, and a `multiple` select takes its own keys and row clicks.

- A pressed Enter on the focused node dispatches a Click when it is no disabled form control and is a `button`, a `summary`, an `input` of type `submit`, `reset` or `button`, or an `a` with `href`; a released Space dispatches it for a `summary`, or for a `button` or an `input` of type `submit`, `reset`, `button`, `checkbox` or `radio` that is no disabled form control, never a link; the app's handlers run, then `handle_click`, so SC 2.1.1 is met by measurement on the stand's buttons.
**Script and framework exposure:**

- A falsy Dioxus value (Bool false, Text `"false"`, Int 0, Float 0.0, None) of one of the bridge's 28 boolean attributes — upstream's `is_bool_attr` set, `disabled`, `hidden` and `inert` among them — removes the attribute on both attribute paths, so an enabled control does not match `:disabled` and `hidden: false` keeps an element laid out and in the tree; a truthy value is still written, and an attribute outside the list holding `false` is written as `"false"`.
**Per-surface keyboard shortcuts:**

- seven_guis CRUD: the person rows are `option`s of a `listbox` by `role` and not focusable; the list `crud-list`, named `People`, is the third CRUD Tab stop and, focused, ArrowDown / ArrowUp / Home / End move the selection as a row's click does; the tree's focus is the list, never the option — the builder reads no `aria-activedescendant` (SC 4.1.2 work outside the tier-0 target), kept unread and pinned by `accessibility_active_descendant_unread`.

- seven_guis Cells: `cells-grid`, named `Cells` by `aria_label` with no role, is one Tab stop; the arrows move `current`, clamped, and bring the cell into view; Enter opens the editor on `current`, focused, and the editor's Enter commits and returns focus to the grid; Tab leaving an open editor commits it; `.cells-grid:focus .cell.current` draws a 2px outline in the stand accent; role and cell semantics stay out, owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line.

title: 7. Screen Reader Support

body: Detail: .andromeda/a11y-plan-detail/screen-reader-support.md — read whole.
**Accessibility tree output:**

- An element's `aria-label`, non-empty after trimming, becomes its `label` (accname §2C), a whitespace-only one naming nothing; an `aria-labelledby` whose targets hold text outranks it (accname 2B), the `aria-label` the fallback when they hold none.

- A `<label>` names the labelable element it is bound to — its `for`-target by id, else its first nested labelable element — by being pushed onto its `labelled_by` after the tree is built, so a label before or after its element both work; a hidden input is named by no label, and an input carrying `aria-labelledby` is named by its targets instead (accname 2B over 2D).

- In a Dioxus document every element node carries its stable element id as AccessKit `author_id`, no `TextRun`, document-root or `Window` node one; on the stand every interactive-role node of the four lean tasks reads a non-empty name and the tree the shell hands the adapter equals the harness's tree node for node; the roles and names the checks expect are stated once, in the shared module's tables — never a second role or name mapping.

- The snapshot model consumes the tree: `DioxusDocument::snapshot` takes each node's role, name, focus and `selected`, `pressed` and `invalid` from `accessibility_tree`, never from the element, and `enabled` (the presence of `disabled`) and `value` from the element, `checked` from a native checkbox's or radio's state, else a checkable role's `toggled`; its text form, parts, diff, MCP results, node-key help and `screenshot` read that model and nothing else — never a second role or name mapping.

- A password input's value reads as the fixed `MASKED_VALUE` where it holds text and `""` where it holds none, its typed text in no snapshot field, tree node or painted frame (blitz-paint paints bullets, and a click places the caret by them), and a file input with a non-empty `value` reads the same marker; the driver refuses a `click` or a `type` as `disabled` where the snapshot's `enabled` reads `Some(false)`, nothing dispatched.

- The actionable-key rule: every element an agent can act on — focusable, carrying an interactive role or an event listener — reads an author key, so its `author_id` is that key and holds under any edit of the code around it; `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` is the check, with no second role mapping, and returns nothing on every stand task; no snapshot field says an element reacts to a click — that reading owned by a `.andromeda/residuals.md` line (target: next).

- On the stand two kinds of control state a role or a state by attribute alone — the CRUD list `listbox` with `option` rows carrying `aria-selected`, and the flight booker's date inputs `aria-invalid`; the stand states no `aria-pressed`, the flight booker's mode a `select` whose options state its choice by `selected`; one gap stands open: the rows are not focusable and the tree's focus is the list, never the option, the missing `aria-activedescendant` kept unread (§5 Per-surface keyboard shortcuts).

- A `multiple` select carries `set_multiselectable` in the tree and its rows read their own client rects in the snapshot, its `value` reading `select_value`, its first chosen option in tree order; an `optgroup` reads `Role::Group`, its non-empty `label` attribute its name, named in the tree and painted as a header of an open list, heavier than a row by weight on every build, a header choosing nothing; what an assistive technology reads of them is not measured.

- A single select reads `ComboBox` and writes `expanded` from its list's open state, reading no `aria-expanded`, and an author's `open` or `aria-expanded` on it steers nothing; the tree's focus stays on the select and its chosen option reads `selected`; the highlighted row is in no snapshot and no tree; the snapshot holds no `expanded` key, an open list's row reading its own `bounds` in the list; what an assistive technology reads of the list is not measured.

The stand at boot reads no `contrast` finding on the four lean tasks in both layout modes, the nodes outside `stand_contrast`'s rows included — and no finding of any kind at boot, `at_boot` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` (below; as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-engine-debts/report.md); a planted low-contrast row reads 2.8490272 against 4.5, equal to `text_contrast`'s own reading (tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_lint.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_lint.rs: — as measured at escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-19-visual-lint/report.md and its evidence/readings.md); the `a11y` leg reads 114 tests over 14 targets, `stand_contrast`'s 7 among them (§9; as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-select-popup/report.md)

- The driver's visual lint leaves a closed select's options and an open list's rows and groups out of its overlap reading in every document, the snapshot giving a closed select's `ListBoxOption` its select's client rect and an open list's row its painted row's bounds: `overlaps` skips such an entry on either side, `Entry.in_select_box` true for an option of a closed select, read through `closed_select_of` and never the role, and for an open list's row or group, read through `select_list_bounds`, so CRUD's `role="option"` rows are not read as a select's and a `multiple` select's rows are linted as usual; `clip_region` takes an open row's region from `visible_region` alone, no `contain: paint` cut; the stand's flight booker at boot reads no `overlap` in both layout modes, `stand_lint`'s `the_stand_at_boot_reads_its_measured_findings` reading `[0, 0, 0, 0]` (packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/lint.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_lint.rs: — as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-engine-debts/report.md)

- `select_popup_painted` reads the highlight and a disabled row as painted against `SelectListView`'s constants and measures the open list's plain pair at the default sheet and at the stand, in both layout modes (tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup_painted.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/select_popup_painted.rs: — as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-select-popup/report.md)

- An open list's rows take one height, the select's font on one line, so a row with a larger authored font clips, a stated limit (docs/capabilities.md: — as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-select-popup/report.md)
- Observed absent — contrast checks · searched: `contrast` over the 15 s05 files

- Browser urlbar focus shows a `#5E9ED6` border and 1px outline (apps/browser/assets/browser.css:)

- Elements with `visibility: hidden` or `collapse` are never hit-test targets (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:)

- A transform whose determinant is 0 or not finite answers `None` from `Node::hit_inner` for the whole subtree, so that subtree takes no hit, an invertible twin hit where it shows, asserted by `hit_non_invertible_transform` in both layout modes (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/hit_non_invertible_transform.rs:) — as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-engine-debts/report.md

title: 2026-10-06-headless-stand — disabled keyed two ways; Dioxus falsy disabled cleared; flight-booker cue checked
body:
## 2026-10-06-headless-stand — disabled keyed two ways; Dioxus falsy disabled cleared; flight-booker cue checked
**Section:** §5 Keyboard Navigation → Focus order per layout (engine) · Script and framework exposure · §8 Cognitive Accessibility → Error recovery
**Change:**
- Focus order: was "focusable if it is not disabled"; now "if its `disabled` attribute does not parse as `true`", and a new bullet: the DISABLED/ENABLED state (`:disabled`) and the click target key on presence, focusability on the parsed bool — `disabled="false"` matches `:disabled` yet stays focusable, a bare `disabled=""` is focusable too.
- Framework exposure: dioxus-native-dom removes a falsy `disabled` / `checked`; its other boolean attributes are still written as `"false"` — for `hidden` that would drop a `hidden: false` node from the tree: recorded, not established.
- Error recovery: the stand check asserts the invalid-date cue without colour (`invalid` class, `disabled` Book it did not carry before); no test asserts a Dioxus control's focusability or Tab order.
**Why:** the headless stand chunk measured `disabled="false"` matching `:disabled` on enabled stand buttons and fixed the Dioxus write (widening on the delegate overseer's word, 2026-10-06, PROVISIONAL). Trap: the focusability path never had the defect — only state, styling and click targeting did.

## 2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity — name sources, carried stable id, Dioxus feature wiring
**Section:** §1 A11y Scope Summary (Dioxus crates · blitz-tests · crate docs) · §2 A11y Strategy (tree build) · §7 Screen Reader Support → Accessibility tree output · citations re-pointed
**Change:**
- §1: was "`accessibility` … forwards to blitz-dom (and blitz-shell in dioxus-native)" and "the Dioxus crates only forward the feature to blitz"; now dioxus-native-dom's feature forwards to blitz-dom and enables its own optional `accesskit`, gating its `accessibility_tree` override, and dioxus-native's forwards to blitz-dom, blitz-shell and dioxus-native-dom. The workspace takes both with `default-features = false`, so a crate gets the feature only by naming it — the seven_guis stand binary names none and builds no platform adapter. blitz-tests builds dioxus-native-dom with `accessibility`.
- §2: the shell builds and refreshes the tree through `Document::accessibility_tree`, so a wrapper's override reaches the platform tree.
- §7: an `aria-label` non-empty after trimming becomes the node's `label` (accname-1.2 §2C); a `<label>` names its bound `<input>` (`for`-target, else first nested) through `labelled_by`, before or after it; in a Dioxus document every element node carries its stable id as `author_id`, no `TextRun` / document-root / `Window` node does; the 15 stand controls carry an HTML-AAM role and a non-empty name in both layout modes, the six inputs named by four `<label for>` and two `aria-label` attributes, the Tab order unchanged.
- 33 citations into the changed files re-pointed by the measured line map.
**Why:** intent §Findings 1's accessibility-tree leg; the six stand inputs had no accessible name because the tree read only text children. The operator chose the name sources (`aria-label` plus `<label>` association) at phase P4. Trap: the windowed stand ships no AccessKit at all — the operator directed a working-route note for it at this wrap.

## 2026-10-06-snapshot-model — the snapshot consumes the accessibility tree
**Section:** §2 A11y Strategy (the `accessibility` feature) · §7 Screen Reader Support → Accessibility tree output · → Platform adapter · §8 Cognitive Accessibility (the flight-booker cue)
**Change:**
- §7 Accessibility tree output: adds the snapshot model as a consumer — `DioxusDocument::snapshot` takes each node's role, name and the focused node from the tree `accessibility_tree` returns, with no second role or name mapping; on the stand every snapshot node's role and name equal its accessibility node's, nothing reads focused at boot and only `back-btn` does after one focus move.

**Why:** the snapshot is the second reader of the tree's role, name and focus, so §7 records it and the rule that it never re-derives them. The §8 sentence was already false since the accessibility-tree-identity chunk and is corrected here, where a second check contradicts it.

## 2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits — the actionable-key rule and its check
**Section:** §2 Feature exposure · §5 Script and framework exposure · §7 Accessibility tree output · → Platform adapter · §8 Error recovery · → Orientation and status cues
**Change:**
- §7 adds the rule: every element an agent can act on — focusable, or an interactive role, or a listener — reads an author key, so its `author_id` holds under any edit around it. `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable` is the check; it takes the role from the accessibility tree with no second mapping, holds a disabled control by its role and a hidden one by focusability or its listener. On the stand it reads empty on the four lean tasks and Home in every state, and 2 · 3 · 676 on the temp converter, circle drawer and cells. CRUD rows (`crud-person-{person.id}`) and Home's cards (`task-card-{slug}`) were keyed by an `id` attribute alone: no `tabindex`, role, focusability or Tab-order change.
- §2: the `accessibility` feature also gates the actionable-key check.
- Eleven line citations re-pointed, and `lib.rs:14-15` added in §2. Two of the eleven, the seven_guis card citations in §8, had already drifted before this chunk and now point at the `TASKS` table and the card markup.
**Why:** the rule is the founder's (the founder, 2026-10-06). Trap for later chunks: never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or a role — that changes the Tab order §5 pins; key the element.

## 2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff — the tree is refreshed on change; the diff reads the snapshot model
**Section:** §2 A11y Strategy → Accessibility tree lifecycle · Feature exposure; §7 → Accessibility tree output; `file:line` citations into five edited files
**Change:**
- Lifecycle: the platform tree is built on InitialTreeRequested and refreshed on change — on a poll that reported work `View::poll` takes the document's changed set (outside the `accessibility` cfg) and, under `accessibility`, rebuilds the tree when the set it took was non-empty (was: "refreshed on poll when the document has changes"; that refresh did not run before this chunk, the flag it read answering false, so the tree was built once). No windowed run witnesses it on the dev host.
- Lifecycle: `changed_nodes` is the engine's changed set — marked by a mutation of an in-document node, a focus or checked change and a text control's input; not by node creation, hover, active, scroll or layout; `has_changes()` true while it is non-empty (was: "documented as the set of changed nodes for updating the accessibility tree").
- Feature exposure: the `accessibility` feature of dioxus-native-dom also gates the snapshot's diff `Snapshot::diff`; four items named by the crate doc (was three).
- Accessibility tree output: the diff is one more reader of the snapshot model, with no second role or name mapping — a text change reported on the element whose accessible name it changes, never as a text-run entry; a hidden element leaving and returning with its descendants; focus moves naming exactly the controls whose `focused` reading moved.
- 17 of 28 citations re-pointed by the measured line map.
**Why:** the chunk made the engine's change flag truthful and the shell drain it, so the refresh the plan described now happens. It is PROVISIONAL, pending the founder at the Epoch 3 boundary — one item with the engine flag contract (the operator, 2026-10-07, at the chunk's plan and at this wrap's escalation: record as provisional). Its windowed witness is owed on the working route's "Stand a11y assertions".
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-07T01-31-03-wrap/

body:
## 2026-10-07-act-by-id — the session library names `accessibility`; both stand binaries compile the tree override, neither an adapter
**Section:** §1 A11y Scope Summary → Dioxus crates
**Change:** the row was "the session library `escher-driver` … names no feature of `dioxus-native-dom` either — it reads no snapshot — so the stand binary's build is unchanged and its `escher-session` host builds no accessibility code; the entry that first reads the snapshot through a session decides the feature then". Now: `escher-driver` names `accessibility` on `dioxus-native-dom`, unconditionally and with no `[features]` table of its own, because its executor reads the snapshot; the feature reaches seven_guis through that edge although seven_guis' own manifest names none, so both its binaries — the windowed `seven_guis_native` and the `escher-session` host — compile dioxus-native-dom's accessibility modules (the `accessibility_tree` override that carries `author_id`, the snapshot model, its text and its diff). Neither builds a platform adapter: `accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` are in neither graph, `accesskit` was already in both through blitz-dom, and the lockfile is byte-identical. A crate gets the feature by naming it or by depending on a crate that names it (was "only by naming it").
**Why:** the entry the row deferred the decision to has run: a driver action returns a diff, and the diff does not exist without the snapshot model. The reach was measured on the dev host's target by five dependency-graph reads before and after the one manifest line. Standing consequence: the stand binary still hands no assistive technology a tree, so a windowed run still proves the boot only; the windowed witness of the tree refresh stays owed where the route carries it.
**Kept:** "the seven_guis stand binary names none … and builds no platform adapter" — true of its own manifest and of both graphs; the statement that the stand's windowed binary builds blitz-shell without `accessibility`.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-07T14-22-35-wrap/

title: 2026-10-10-snapshot-states — the tree states selected, toggled and invalid, and the snapshot takes them from it
body:
## 2026-10-10-snapshot-states — the tree states selected, toggled and invalid, and the snapshot takes them from it
**Section:** §2 A11y Strategy → Role derivation · §3 → A11y testing tool pick · §4 → Per-component pattern catalog · §7 → Accessibility tree output (the snapshot-model bullet)
**Change:**
- §2: gains the builder's three state reads, on every element whatever its role, each value trimmed and compared exactly in lower case — `aria-selected` `true` / `false` → `selected`; `aria-pressed` `true` / `false` / `mixed` → `toggled`; `aria-invalid` `true` / `grammar` / `spelling` → `invalid`, an absent, empty or `false` value nothing, any other value `Invalid::True`. `TRUE` reads unrecognized. `aria-checked` is not read, so a node's `toggled` is exactly its `aria-pressed` reading. A role that does not support an attribute reads it as one that does.
- §3: gains the state check — one stated table per attribute, its row count asserted, both layout modes — run by the workspace test leg and per package; the `a11y` leg stays three files.
- §4: the catalog gains "ARIA state attributes"; `aria-checked` sets none of the three, so an ARIA checkbox or switch states no checked reading through it.
- §7: was "the tree gives an element node no value, checked or disabled property, so the snapshot reads those three from the element"; that stands, and beside it the tree now gives `selected`, `toggled` and `invalid`, which the snapshot takes from the tree and never from the element — `NodeState` at seven fields, a mixed toggle reading `pressed` false and a grammar or spelling error reading invalid, three text tokens after `value=` and before `focused`, each stand reading equal to its accessibility node's.
**Why:** ratified by the founder (2026-10-10, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer; confirmed by him at this wrap's card, relayed the same way): the builder writes the three states on the node. State is what the tree exists to carry, and one parser of each attribute keeps the snapshot and the tree from disagreeing.
**Kept:** what an assistive technology reads of the three is not measured; the windowed witness and the ARIA checkbox reading are each owned by a route entry.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-10-10T17-47-57-wrap/

The actionable-key check still returns nothing.
- §7, the stable-id bullet: "the 15 interactive controls carry … a non-empty accessible name" stands for those 15; an element outside them now carries an interactive role — the list reads `ListBox` with the accessible name `""` — so not every interactive-role element on the stand is named.

**Why:** the stand's tasks state the three states so a snapshot can read them; the roles and attributes are the operator's answers at the chunk's plan forks.

## 2026-10-31-engine-debts — a `multiple` select's keys and row clicks
**Section:** §5 Focus restoration (a11y-plan.md; keyboard-navigation.md: keyboard-focus-restoration); §5 Keyboard handling (a11y-plan.md; keyboard-navigation.md: keyboard-handling); §5 Test harness pattern (keyboard-navigation.md: keyboard-harness)
**Change:**
- Was a `multiple` select not modelled and taking no key; now it takes its own keys and row clicks.
- Keys, on one focused and no disabled form control: ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End alone choose that row alone, with Shift span from the anchor, with Ctrl or Meta move the current row and change nothing. A Space with no typed text standing flips the current row and with text standing joins it; a character with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta chooses its match alone. Disabled rows are never chosen; Ctrl+A is not modelled. Shift with no cursor yet spans from the last chosen row, so a set the markup seeds is stepped and spanned from it.
- Clicks: `click_select_row` behind `handle_click`'s `option` arm, in every document. A disabled select stops it; otherwise it focuses the select and clears the typeahead and the text selection; a plain click chooses the row alone, Ctrl or Meta flips it, Shift spans, and a disabled row changes nothing.
- Was an option not clicked; now an option of a closed single select, under a group too, is not clicked.
- A `multiple` write or removal records the select (`record_select_of_multiple_write`), so removal settles it to one; `set_option_selectedness` leaves a `multiple` select's other options alone.

## 3. A11y Assertion Harness Contract

**A11y testing tool pick:** accessibility assertions are Rust tests in blitz-tests over the AccessKit tree.
- Tests call `document.build_accessibility_tree()` after `resolve` and match `tree_update.nodes` with `test_that` matchers on `role()` and `is_hidden()` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_hidden.rs:9-26)
- An `assert_role(html, element_id, expected)` helper maps the element's `NodeId` to an AccessKit `NodeId(node_id.as_u64())` and compares roles (tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_roles.rs:39-72)
- An `unknown_tags(html)` helper lists the `html_tag` of nodes with `Role::Unknown` (tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_roles.rs:16-37)
- The test harness builds blitz-dom with the accessibility feature (packages/blitz-test-harness/Cargo.toml:15)
- accesskit_xplat ships a doc-comment usage example, not tests (packages/accesskit_xplat/src/lib.rs:13-86)

**Focus management test harness:**
- The harness exposes focused and hovered node queries (packages/blitz-test-harness/src/inspect.rs:107-115)

**Keyboard test harness:** keyboard-event and Tab-order navigation tests are observed absent — see §5 (Test harness pattern).

**Contrast verification harness:** contrast checks are observed absent — see §6.

**CI integration:** accessibility checks in CI are observed absent — see §9.
